brief_summary:
This is an observational clinical study. It does not give new treatments to participants. Researchers want to learn how sleep gets better or worse after laparoscopic gallbladder removal surgery. Sleep problems are common after surgery. Some people may recover their sleep faster than others. Researchers will look at whether sleep recovery differs between women and men. They will also check how sex-related hormone levels connect with sleep changes.

About 58 participants will join this study.

Key requirements to take part:

* Aged 18 to 65 years old
* Scheduled for laparoscopic gallbladder removal under general anesthesia
* Able to give informed consent and finish all study tasks
* Can tolerate repeated blood draws
* No long-term sleep-affecting medicine use in the past one month
* Major organs work normally

People cannot join if they:

* Are younger than 18 years or older than 65 years
* Are pregnant or breastfeeding
* Have mental health or cognitive conditions that stop study participation
* Have problems that make repeated blood collection unsafe
* Have severe organ diseases or recent major injury or surgery
* Have alcohol or drug dependence

What happens for each participant:

1. Before surgery: Participants sign consent forms. Staff collect basic health information. Participants wear a sleep-recording device called polysomnography (PSG) overnight. Participants fill out a short sleep diary each morning. Fasting blood samples are collected the next morning to measure hormone levels.
2. On surgery day: Standard hospital care goes forward. Staff record surgery-related information. PSG sleep recording, sleep diary, and morning blood draw are repeated.
3. First and second days after surgery: The same sleep recording, sleep diary, and morning fasting blood collection continue for two more nights.

Researchers compare sleep measurements across four nights. These measurements come from both PSG machine readings and participants' self-reported sleep diaries. Researchers also compare hormone level changes between female and male participants.

Possible benefits: Participants receive objective feedback on their own sleep and hormone results. If test values show clear concerns, researchers share these findings with their clinical care team. No direct treatment benefit is guaranteed.

Possible risks: This is a low-risk study. Small risks may include mild pain, bruising at blood draw sites, or temporary light-headedness from blood collection. Filling out short diaries may bring minor tiredness. All personal data will be kept private. Participants can leave the study at any time with no penalty.
primary_outcomes: Wake After Sleep Onset (WASO), measured in minutes by polysomnography
Proportions of Rapid Eye Movement (REM) Sleep, Non-Rapid Eye Movement (NREM) Sleep, and Wakefulness measured by polysomnography
Proportions of N1, N2, and N3 stages of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep measured by polysomnography
Sleep Onset Latency (SOL), measured in minutes by polysomnography
Total Sleep Time (TST), measured in minutes by polysomnography
Sleep Efficiency (SE), measured as a percentage by polysomnography
Serum Testosterone Concentration
Serum Progesterone Concentration
Serum Cortisol Concentration
Serum Estradiol (E2) Concentration
title: Perioperative Sleep Recovery Trajectories in Patients of Different Sexes Undergoing Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary: This randomized controlled pilot study evaluated the effects of auricular electroacupuncture and auricular acupuncture combined with health education on pain management in adults diagnosed with leprosy or who had completed pharmacological treatment. Participants were randomly allocated to three parallel groups: auricular electroacupuncture plus health education, auricular acupuncture plus health education, or an active control group receiving transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS). The primary outcome was pain intensity, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale. Secondary outcomes included functional mobility, upper limb function, physical disability, and quality of life. Assessments were performed at baseline and after the intervention period.
primary_outcomes: Pain Intensity Assessed by the Visual Analog Scale
title: Auricular Electroacupuncture and Auricular Acupuncture With Health Education for Pain in Leprosy

brief_summary:
Sarcopenia is an age-related condition characterized by loss of muscle strength and muscle mass, which may contribute to reduced physical function and independence in older adults. Resistance exercise is recommended as an important component of sarcopenia management. Elastic resistance training is a simple and practical form of resistance exercise that can be performed with minimal equipment and may be suitable for older adults living in long-term care facilities.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated whether adding elastic resistance training to routine physical exercise improves handgrip strength in older adults with sarcopenia. Participants were assigned to either routine physical exercise combined with elastic resistance training or routine physical exercise alone for 8 weeks. The primary outcome was change in handgrip strength. Secondary outcomes included physical performance, mobility, gait speed, and body composition.
primary_outcomes: Change in Handgrip Strength
title: Effect of Elastic Resistance Training on Handgrip Strength in Older Adults With Sarcopenia

brief_summary:
This study aims to assess and evaluate the clinical efficacy of an intensified form of Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS) compared to standard conservative treatment for low anterior resection syndrome (LARS). A syndrome with symptoms such as faecal incontinence (FI), urgency to defecate and frequent bowel movements. Focus will be mainly on patients with significant faecal incontinence.

Participants will be randomized into 2 groups: Standard Care with bowel regulation or to High Intensive PTNS for 6 weeks.

Every treatment session will be at the clinic and take 30 minutes.

Standard care PTNS participants will have nurse contact once per week for 6 weeks

High Intensive PTNS participants will start with 5 sessions per week, which will the be phased out to 2 sessions per weeks during the 6 week period.

Follow up visits to the clinic will be at 3, 6 and 12 months after completion of study.

Patients in the Standard group whose symtoms have not improved significantly, will be given the option to try the High Intensive treatment option.
primary_outcomes: Reduction in Low Anterior Resection Syndrome Score
title: Efficacy of a Novel High Intensive Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation on Faecal Incontinence in Patients With Low Anterior Resection Cancer Syndrome After Rectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated a culturally adapted mindfulness-based intervention for Pakistani parents of children with autism spectrum disorder. Sixty-eight parents were randomly assigned to one of three groups: a mindfulness-based intervention (n = 23), an active psychoeducation comparator (n = 23), or a waitlist control (n = 22). The mindfulness-based intervention and psychoeducation programs were delivered in eight weekly group sessions. Participants completed assessments at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and one month after the intervention. The study examined changes in mindfulness, self-compassion, and parenting stress among parents of children with autism spectrum disorder.

title: Mindfulness-Based Intervention for Parents of Autistic Children in Pakistan

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn which factors can predict how well lutetium-177 PSMA therapy works in people with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). This therapy is a radioactive medicine (Pluvicto) given into a vein.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can scan results, radiation dose measurements, and blood test results predict which participants will have their prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level drop by half or more?
* Can the same results predict how long participants live without their cancer getting worse?

All participants receive Pluvicto as part of their regular medical care. Taking part in the study does not change their treatment.

Participants will:

* Receive up to 6 Pluvicto treatments, about every 6 weeks, as part of regular care
* Have a PSMA PET/CT scan (an imaging test that shows where the cancer is) before treatment and after the last treatment, as part of regular care
* Have 3 SPECT/CT scans after each treatment (at 3 to 4 hours, 24 hours, and 5 days) to measure how much radiation reached the tumors and organs, as part of regular care
* Give 1 extra blood sample (10 ml) after each treatment to measure tumor DNA in the blood. It is taken from the same needle stick as routine blood tests.
* Fill in a quality of life questionnaire (SF-36) before treatment and after every second treatment, during their hospital stay
* Have check-ups every 4 to 6 months after treatment ends

Researchers will also use existing medical records of people who started Pluvicto at the hospital before the study began.
primary_outcomes: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response
Progression-free survival (PFS)
title: Predictive Factors for Response to Lutetium-177 PSMA Radioligand Therapy in Patients With Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer

brief_summary:
Submental fat accumulation, commonly known as a "double chin," is a frequent aesthetic complaint affecting the lower face and neck and is often associated with aging, weight gain, or a genetic predisposition (1). It develops from excess fat deposition in the superficial (pre-platysmal) and deep (post-platysmal) compartments of the neck (2), and can persist even in individuals of normal body weight owing to localized adipocyte hypertrophy that is resistant to diet and exercise (1). A large United States survey of adults aged 18-65 years found that 47% of respondents reported being bothered by the appearance of the area underneath their chin (3), and submental fullness has been consistently linked to lowered self-esteem and negative self-perception that motivate patients to seek treatment (1).

Several objective grading systems have been developed to standardize submental fat assessment. The Clinician-Reported and Patient-Reported Submental Fat Rating Scales, validated during the pivotal ATX-101 clinical trials, and an ethnicity-specific reference-photograph set derived from this scale later achieved inter-rater kappa values between 0.70 and 0.91 (4). Newer severity tools, including the Clinician Submental Fat Scale (5) and the Clinician-Chin Assessment Tool (6), have also been used to stratify patients before enrollment in pharmacologic trials.

Management options for submental fat span a wide spectrum. Injectable deoxycholic acid lipolysis has produced a significant reduction of submental fat in randomized placebo-controlled trials and meta-analyses, with a tolerable and mostly transient adverse-event profile, although a potential industry-sponsorship bias has been raised across the available trials (2). A newer injectable lipolytic agent achieved comparable improvement on clinician- and patient-reported scales, together with objective volume reduction on magnetic resonance imaging, in a large randomized Chinese cohort (7).

Cryolipolysis has similarly demonstrated efficacy for submental fat reduction, with pooled data from multiple pre-post studies showing a mean fat-thickness reduction of about 2.8 mm and a favorable safety profile (8), a finding corroborated by three-dimensional imaging analyses showing measurable volumetric loss and high patient satisfaction (9). Other non-invasive energy-based approaches, including combined focused-electrical-stimulation and radiofrequency devices, have been shown histologically to induce adipocyte apoptosis in the submental region (10). For patients with marked skin laxity or advanced neck-laxity grades, surgical techniques such as submental liposuction with platysma plication or resection remain the treatment of choice, as demonstrated in a recent submentoplasty cohort (10).

Given the absence of local Egyptian data comparing the full spectrum of double chin management options and the lack of information on the true burden of this condition among Egyptian patients, this cohort study is designed to systematically evaluate patients with submental fullness at Assiut University Hospital and to compare the effectiveness, safety, and patient satisfaction of the different available modalities, in order to generate evidence-based, locally relevant treatment guidance
primary_outcomes: The degree of reduction in submental fat
title: Evaluation and Management of Double Chin Submental Fat at Assiut University Hospital

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effect of omega-3 enriched egg supplementation combined with nutrition education in pregnant women with Chronic Energy Deficiency (CED).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does omega-3 egg supplementation combined with nutrition education improve maternal nutritional status (nutrient intake, anthropometry, serum DHA, EPA, IL-6, serum albumin, ferritin, knowledge, and Health Belief Model constructs) in pregnant women with CED compared to nutrition education alone?
2. Does this combined intervention improve pregnancy and neonatal outcomes (gestational age, preterm birth, postpartum hemorrhage, newborn anthropometry, and breast milk fatty acid profile) compared to nutrition education alone?

Researchers will compare the intervention group (receiving omega-3 enriched eggs and nutrition education) to a control group (receiving nutrition education only) to evaluate these effects.

Participants will:

1. Attend structured nutrition education sessions (both groups)
2. Consume daily omega-3 enriched eggs during the intervention period (intervention group only)Undergo baseline and follow-up assessments including blood sampling (DHA, EPA, IL-6, albumin, ferritin), anthropometric measurements, and dietary questionnaires
3. Provide post-delivery and neonatal data, as well as breast milk samples after delivery for fatty acid profiling

Newborn Birth Weight (gram)
Maternal serum EPA level (ug/mL)

title: Omega-3 Egg Intervention and Nutrition Education in Pregnant Women

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a daily unflavored powdered multivitamin (EllaOla Kids Essentials) improves mood and behavior in children aged 4 to 11 who are picky eaters and experience behavioral challenges. Researchers will also look at whether the multivitamin affects overall health, well-being, nutrition, and serum vitamin levels, and whether it is safe and well tolerated.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do more parents of children taking the multivitamin report a clinically meaningful improvement in their child's overall mood and behavior after 12 weeks than parents of children taking a placebo? Does the multivitamin change parent-reported emotional reactivity, overall health and well-being, and nutrition over 12 weeks? In children who take part in optional at-home blood testing, does the multivitamin improve serum vitamin D and vitamin B12 levels?

Researchers will compare the multivitamin to a placebo (a look-alike powder made of tapioca fiber that contains no vitamins) to see if it improves mood and behavior.

Participants will:

Be randomly assigned to receive either the multivitamin or the placebo. Neither the families nor the study team will know which one the child gets.

Have a parent or caregiver mix the powder into the child's food or drink once a day at home for 12 weeks.

Have a parent or caregiver complete short online questionnaires about the child's mood, behavior, health, and nutrition at baseline and at Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12, using a smartphone app. All study visits are remote.

Choose whether to do an optional at-home blood collection at the start and at Week 12.

Choose whether to continue in an optional 12-week open-label extension (Weeks 12-24), where all children, including those who were on placebo, receive the multivitamin.
interventions: EllaOla Kids Essentials Unflavored Powdered Multivitamin
primary_outcomes: Proportion of PGI-C Responders on the Overall Mood and Behavior Item
title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial Evaluating the Effect of an Unflavored Powdered Multivitamin on Behavior and Overall Health in Children Aged 4-11 Years

brief_summary: MASLD (Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease), is a chronic liver condition marked by excessive fat buildup (steatosis) in liver cells, linked to at least one metabolic risk factor like obesity, type 2 diabetes, high blood lipids, or hypertension. Vitamin E serves as a recommended antioxidant therapy for select MASLD patients. It reduces liver inflammation markers such as ALT and AST, alongside benefits in steatosis and MASH resolution. Silymarin has clinical evidence supports its use as an adjunctive hepatoprotective agent due to antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic effects.

brief_summary:
Coronary artery disease occurs when fatty deposits (plaques) build up inside the arteries that supply blood to the heart. Some plaques remain stable, while others continue to grow or become more likely to rupture, which can lead to a heart attack. Identifying plaques that are at higher risk of progression could help doctors provide earlier and more personalized treatment.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether combining information about blood flow within the coronary arteries with information about a person's biological response to blood flow can improve prediction of plaque growth. Participants undergoing treatment for coronary artery disease will have a specialized heart scan to assess blood flow patterns around plaques in their coronary arteries. Researchers will also collect blood samples to study cells that line blood vessels and investigate how these cells respond to blood flow forces.

The study will follow participants over time to determine whether plaques are more likely to progress in individuals who show a stronger biological response to abnormal blood flow. The findings may help researchers develop new ways to identify patients at higher risk of future heart problems and support the development of more personalized approaches to prevention and treatment of coronary artery disease.
interventions: Endothelial cell isolation from peripheral blood sample
primary_outcomes: Percentage change in plaque burden over 12 months
ECFC isolation from peripheral blood sample
title: Predicting Plaque Growth Using Blood Flow Stress Markers: A Proof-of-Concept Study

brief_summary:
Tetralogy of Fallot is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease. Management strategies vary between primary repair and staged approaches including palliative surgery. The development of pulmonary arteries is a key determinant in surgical decision-making.

This multicenter retrospective observational study aims to evaluate the evolution of pulmonary artery dimensions using the Nakata index at key stages of patient management (birth, palliative surgery, and complete repair). The goal is to assess its predictive value in optimizing surgical strategy and improving outcomes in patients with Tetralogy of Fallot or pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect.
primary_outcomes: Nakata index evolution and predictive value
title: Volution of Pulmonary Artery Dimensions in Tetralogy of Fallot

brief_summary: This post-marketing, multi-center, prospective, single-arm, observational study will be conducted across 3 clinical sites in China and enroll no more than 50 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. After clinical site initiation, each study site was permitted to enroll up to 2 roll-in cases to allow operators to familiarize themselves with the Nordica® cryoballoon and standardize procedural techniques. A competitive enrollment method will be adopted to recruit up to 50 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The Nordica® cryoballoon will be employed for pulmonary vein isolation during the procedure. A 6-month follow-up assessment is scheduled at the following time points: the index hospitalization period (days 0-3), and post-procedure follow-up time points at 30 days, 3 months, and 6 months.
primary_outcomes: Composite endpoint of 30-day postoperative complications
Incidence of freedom from atrial arrhythmia at 6 months postoperatively
title: Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation

brief_summary:
Dietary patterns and physical inactivity common in Western societies have been associated with chronic low-grade inflammation and an increased risk of non-communicable health conditions. Fruits and vegetables contain polyphenols and other bioactive compounds that may have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and may influence inflammatory biomarkers.

This study will evaluate the effects of increased consumption of a fruit juice on inflammatory biomarkers and exercise capacity in adults with mildly elevated inflammation. Approximately 40 participants will be randomly assigned to consume one of two fruit juice interventions daily for approximately 2 weeks. Changes in C-reactive protein (CRP) and exercise capacity, assessed using a 6-minute walk test, will be evaluated before and after the intervention and compared between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Changes in the biomarker C-reactive protein (CRP) level
title: What is the Effect of Increased Consumption of Fruit Juice on Exercise Capacity and Inflammatory Biomarkers?

We hypothesized that early patellar traction could improve knee stiffness, leading to better knee function. The primary outcome was performance-based knee tests, and the secondary outcome is knee function in children.

brief_summary: This single-centre prospective study compared three nasal packing materials used after endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) in adults with chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps: a chitosan-based bioresorbable pack (PosiSep X), an absorbable gelatin sponge (Spongostan) and a non-absorbable polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) sinus pack. Sixty patients were allocated in three consecutive blocks of 20 by order of enrolment, with the order of materials determined by drawing lots (first 20 PosiSep X, next 20 Spongostan, last 20 PVA sinus pack); all materials were removed 48 hours after surgery. The study evaluated postoperative pain (visual analogue scale) with the pack in place and at removal, postoperative bleeding within the first 24 hours, nasal obstruction (NOSE score) on postoperative day 2 and at 1 month, and endoscopic adhesion and mucopurulent discharge scores at postoperative weeks 1 and 4.
interventions: Osseous polyvinyl alcohol sinus pack (EON Meditech)

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate and compare the efficacy of space-correction kinesio taping and neural technique kinesio taping-when added to a home exercise program-versus placebo taping with exercise in individuals with ulnar neuropathy at the elbow.

Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow is the second most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper extremity. It leads to symptoms such as numbness and tingling in the fourth and fifth digits, hand muscle weakness, and reduced manual dexterity, which negatively impact quality of life. Conservative treatment options include activity modification, nerve gliding exercises, and kinesio taping. Although kinesio taping is widely used in conditions like carpal tunnel syndrome, evidence regarding the comparative efficacy of different taping techniques in ulnar nerve entrapment remains limited.

In this study, eligible participants will be randomly assigned to three groups:

Space-Correction Kinesio Taping + Exercise Group Neural Technique Kinesio Taping + Exercise Group Placebo Kinesio Taping + Exercise Group The taping intervention will be administered over 3 weeks for a total of 3 sessions (1 session per week, with tape applied for 3 days followed by a 4-day tape-free interval). All participants will receive activity modification education and perform home ulnar nerve gliding exercises twice daily (10 repetitions per session) for 3 weeks. Outcome evaluations-including symptom severity, clinical parameters, and electrophysiological measurements-will be conducted at baseline, at the end of week 3 (post-treatment), and at the 3-month follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for Daytime Pain
title: Comparison of Kinesio Taping Techniques in Ulnar Nerve Entrapment

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the long-term outcomes and recovery of adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) with sepsis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Which patient-related, infection-related and centre-level factors (for example type of pathogen, time to adequate antibiotic therapy, and local sepsis management practices) are associated with poor quality of life six months after ICU admission for sepsis?
* How do these factors influence other patient-centred outcomes, such as mortality, psychological and cognitive recovery, functional status and return to work?

This is an international, multicentre, prospective observational cohort study. It will consecutively enrol adult patients (18 years or older) admitted to participating ICUs with sepsis, diagnosed by the treating clinician at ICU admission and, where locally available, meeting Sepsis-3 criteria.

Participants will:

* have clinical data collected from their medical records at ICU admission, on day 7 and at ICU discharge (infection characteristics, organ support, antibiotic therapy, delirium, rehabilitation and centre organisation);
* be followed at 28 days (medical record review, or telephone contact if already discharged) and contacted by telephone at 3 months and 6 months after ICU admission for structured assessment of quality of life, psychological and cognitive recovery, functional status, return to work and healthcare utilisation.

The study plans to enrol 600 patients in participating ICUs across several countries, coordinated by Geneva University Hospitals (HUG).

Findings will help identify modifiable factors that may improve long-term recovery and guide future interventions for sepsis survivors.
primary_outcomes: Health-related Quality of Life
title: Long-Term Recovery and Quality of Life in Sepsis Survivors

brief_summary: This randomized, sham-controlled, exploratory clinical trial will evaluate the efficacy and safety of HeLaXON, an investigational low-dose radiation therapy device, in patients with mild Alzheimer's disease dementia. A total of 30 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either low-dose whole-brain radiation therapy or a sham procedure using the same device. Participants in the treatment group will receive 0.04 Gy per session twice weekly for 3 weeks, for a total of 6 sessions and a cumulative dose of 0.24 Gy. Participants in the sham group will undergo the same device procedures without radiation delivery. Participants and outcome assessors will remain blinded to treatment assignment. Changes in cognitive function, dementia severity, daily functioning, and amyloid burden will be evaluated at 6 and 12 months after treatment. Safety will be assessed throughout the study. Exploratory blood biomarkers, including plasma Aβ42/40 ratio, p-tau217, and Aβ oligomer, will also be evaluated.

brief_summary:
Researchers are looking for new treatments for pain. While there are many approved treatments for pain, the treatments do not work well for everyone. People can also become addicted to certain pain medicines. Researchers designed a trial medicine called MK-6916 to treat pain.

The goal of the trial is to learn if at least 1 dose of MK-6916 works better than placebo to lessen pain. A placebo looks like the trial medicine but has no trial medicine in it. Using a placebo helps researchers better understand the effects of the trial medicine.

brief_summary:
This retrospective observational study evaluates the outcomes of a multifactorial drinkable nutraceutical combined with oral minoxidil, compared with oral minoxidil monotherapy, in women with female pattern hair loss (FPHL) treated in routine clinical practice.

Data were collected from a cohort of women with FPHL (Ludwig or Olsen grade I) who received either oral minoxidil alone or oral minoxidil plus the nutraceutical for 6 months. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and at 6 months. The main assessment was standardized phototrichoscopy in the frontal region. Patient-reported outcomes included a hair-specific adaptation of the Skindex-29 quality-of-life questionnaire and a treatment perception questionnaire. Adverse events were also recorded.

brief_summary:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs), which occur in seasonal outbreaks. Among the adult population, immunocompromised individuals, particularly lung transplant recipients and recipients of allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplants (HSCTs), are at the highest risk of severe ARI. RSV can also cause prolonged inflammation of the airways, leading to persistent deterioration in lung function. Thus, in lung transplant recipients, RSV is a major cause of chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), the leading cause of lung transplant failure and mortality beyond the first post-transplant year. In recipients of ACSH, RSV infection is associated with the onset and/or worsening of bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome, which leads to increased mortality. Preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and its short- and long-term consequences in these populations is therefore a key priority.

Three inactivated RSV vaccines, targeting the RSV fusion glycoprotein in its pre-fusion conformation (RSVpreF), have recently been approved for use in adults. These comprise two recombinant protein vaccines - one with an adjuvant (RSVpreF3-AS01, Arexvy®, GSK) and one without (RSVpreF, Abrysvo®, Pfizer) - and one mRNA vaccine. Although these vaccines have demonstrated their safety, immunogenicity and efficacy (reducing the risk of RSV-related IMRI by approximately 80-85 per cent) in adults aged 60 and over, the pivotal trials excluded immunocompromised patients.

To date, there is limited data on the efficacy, immunogenicity and tolerability of these vaccines in high-risk immunocompromised populations, such as recipients of bone marrow transplants and allogeneic stem cell transplants. Real-world studies suggest that RSV vaccines may reduce the risk of RSV-associated acute respiratory infection and hospitalisations in elderly immunocompromised adults. With regard to immunogenicity, the available cohort studies, conducted on small sample sizes, indicate that the vaccine response is heterogeneous and, overall, lower than that observed in immunocompetent older people. Preliminary data suggest that booster vaccination regimens may be necessary to optimise the immune response in these populations.

Given the significant morbidity associated with RSV in recipients of bone marrow transplants and allogeneic stem cell transplants, it is a priority to assess the immunogenicity and safety profile of RSV vaccines, and to determine the optimal vaccination schedule for these high-risk, immunocompromised populations.

The investigators hypothesise that the immune response to RSV vaccines in severely immunocompromised TP and ACSH recipients is weaker than in immunocompetent older adults, and that enhanced vaccination strategies may be required. In this study, two vaccination strategies will be evaluated in these populations:

* a single dose of the adjuvanted RSVpreF3-AS01 vaccine (Arexvy®),
* or a booster regimen comprising two doses of the non-adjuvanted RSVpreF vaccine (Abrysvo®), administered one month apart.
primary_outcomes: RSVpreF-binding antibody response to each of the two RSV vaccine strategies in two distinct subcohorts (LTR and HSCTR)
title: Immunogenicity and Safety of Two Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Strategies in Lung and Allogeneic Haematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipients: A Phase 2 Trial

brief_summary: This study will develop and evaluate a metaverse-based infection control room of errors education program (META-ICR) for nursing students. The study will compare this program with a physical patient room arranged with the same infection control situations. The study will include approximately 110 first-year nursing students at Çankırı Karatekin University in Türkiye. Students will be assigned by chance to either the META-ICR group or the physical room of errors group. Both groups will examine the same patient scenario and identify appropriate and inappropriate infection control practices. Topics will include hand hygiene, protective equipment, isolation precautions, handling of clean and contaminated materials, waste and linen management, and urinary drainage systems. Students in the META-ICR group will record their observations and care decisions through a web-based interface. Students in the physical room group will use paper forms. Both groups will receive feedback with the same educational content and participate in a 15-minute guided discussion after the activity. Activities will take place under similar supervision in university laboratory settings. The study will compare infection control knowledge, perceptions of the metaverse, and satisfaction with learning between the groups. Knowledge will be assessed before education, immediately after the educational session and guided discussion, and four weeks later to assess retention. Metaverse perceptions will be assessed before and immediately after education. Learning satisfaction will be assessed after education. All research questionnaires and knowledge tests will be completed on paper in both groups. The findings will help determine how an interactive virtual room compares with a physical room of errors for teaching infection control to nursing students.

brief_summary: Episodic memory allows us to project ourselves back in time to mentally re-experience the past in vivid detail. This remarkable feat helps to define our personal identities and enables context-appropriate predictions that guide adaptive behavior. Unfortunately, episodic memory loss is a common cognitive consequence of neurological disease, psychiatric disorders, and normative aging, that reflects dysfunction in the hippocampus and the neocortical network to which it connects. This decline can present along a range of severity that spans an impoverished ability to recollect fine-grained event details, e.g., the color of the shirt your spouse was wearing at a birthday party, to forgetting course-grained event details, e.g., having attended a birthday party last weekend. Treating these kinds of memory loss remains challenging because interventions must target information that is definitionally idiosyncratic. However, recent methodological and theoretical advances in cognitive neuroscience reveal novel strategies that may solve this problem. Evidence from behavioral, neuroimaging, and computational modeling studies suggest that the degree to which episodic memories overlap in the hippocampus can be modified in a predictable, experience-dependent manner. Specifically, strong concurrent reactivation of multiple memories can enhance recall of coarse-grained episodic information by increasing hippocampal integration. Conversely, coupling strong and moderate reactivation of memories can enhance recall of fine-grained episodic information be increasing hippocampal differentiation. Consistent with this idea, recent evidence suggests that using a smartphone to record and subsequently replay real-world memory cues can indeed improve episodic memory by reducing representational overlap among memories in the hippocampus. Against this background, this proposal is organized around two primary aims. First, we seek to establish smartphone-guided memory reactivation protocols that selectively promote integration and differentiation of real-world episodic memories in the hippocampus. Experiments in this aim will specifically ask whether unstructured and structured (in terms of narrative, space, and time) reactivation can be used to achieve these outcomes. Second, we will ask whether the benefits of memory reactivation are associated with behavioral and representational costs. Experiments in this aim will probe for undesirable downsides that accompany, or potentially explain, reactivation-based improvements in episodic memory. Our approach combines smartphone technology, pattern-based analysis of functional neuroimaging data, and careful characterization of recall data with neurocognitive theory inspired by computational models of learning mechanisms. Achieving our aims will establish an empirical foundation on which future interventions can be built to systematically target real-world episodic memories at a level of abstraction, i.e., fine-grained vs. coarse-grained detail, that is appropriate for the severity of memory loss.
interventions: Participants use a smartphone to replay self-generated autobiographical memory cues.

title: Real-World Episodic Memory

brief_summary:
With a mortality rate of over 13% in the neuro-intensive care unit, 86% of which are related to the withdrawal of active treatment, predicting a reliable neurological prognosis is of paramount importance in neuro-intensive care to help clinicians inform family members appropriately and tailor care to the patient's presumed wishes. This also helps justify aggressive resuscitation in patients with a presumed good prognosis and, conversely, avoid keeping patients with a poor neurological prognosis alive against their presumed wishes.

Current guidelines recommend multimodal neuro-prognostication, in which the clinician synthesizes prognostic data from the clinical examination, EEG, plasma or CSF biomarkers, and imaging to collaboratively develop an individualized prognosis, even though no study has evaluated the quality of this multimodal prognosis. Furthermore, existing variations depending on the nosological context make this approach complex and likely difficult to replicate.

Brain MRI is an important tool for neuroprognostics in patients with neurological injuries, and for this reason it is commonly used in clinical practice as part of this multimodal approach.

More specifically, brain MRI with diffusion tensor sequences is a validated prognostic tool in post-anoxic coma and traumatic brain injury, as well as, more recently, in subarachnoid hemorrhage, strokes, and hypoglycemia. However, it has not yet been compared to multimodal neuroprognostics performed by the clinician.

The primary objective is to compare the prognostic performance of two prescribing clinicians with diffusion tensor MRI before and after the MRI scan is performed.

Primary outcome measure: to compare the prognostic performance regarding unfavorable outcomes (Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended \< 5) at 12 months between the two prescribing clinicians and diffusion tensor MRI before and after the MRI scan is performed.

A secondary objective will be, among other things, to study the informational gain provided by MRI in improving clinicians' predictions after receiving the MRI results.

Intensive care clinicians constitute the target population. These are clinicians caring for an intensive care patient with a brain injury who order a brain MRI for prognostic purposes as part of patient care and multimodal neuroprognostics.

On the day of the MRI, two clinicians will complete the research questionnaire assessing the patient's prognosis the day before or a few hours before the MRI (on the same day). Then, as soon as the MRI results are available, the same two clinicians will complete the same questionnaire assessing the patient's prognosis after reviewing the MRI results. Patient data regarding the pathology and prognostic factors will be collected at this time.

Finally, surviving patients will be interviewed at 1 year regarding their independence using the Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE) and their quality of life using the Medical Outcomes Study Short Form General Health Survey (SF-12) via a telephone call.

We plan to include 220 patients and approximately 70 clinicians across 8 recruiting centers over a 2-year enrollment period. With a 12-month follow-up period, the total duration of the study will be 3 years.

The statistical analysis will include a description of clinicians' ability to distinguish patient prognosis by measuring the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, or AUC. The prediction concerns an unfavorable outcome, defined as a GOSE score of 1 to 4. Since we had no pre-study data on clinicians' performance in predicting an unfavorable outcome at the time of a prognostic MRI, the inclusion target was set based on data from a previous study at 220 patients, which corresponds to the number of patients we planned to enroll over a 2-year period.
primary_outcomes: Clinicians' ROC curve for predicting unfavorable patient outcomes at 12 months before MRI (Glasgow Outcome Scale Extended (GOSE <5)
title: Description of Clinicians' Predictive Abilities Before and After a Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI)

brief_summary: Chronic neck pain is a common health condition that causes disability and functional limitations, and while clinicians frequently rely on patient-reported questionnaires to assess symptoms, it remains unclear how accurately these self-reported measures reflect actual physical capacity. Ultimately, the findings will clarify whether self-reported questionnaires are sufficient for evaluating physical capacity or if objective performance testing should be routinely integrated into clinical practice

The purpose of this study is to find out whether high-flow tracheal oxygen (HFTO) delivered at flows greater than 60 L/min can increase end-expiratory lung volume (EELV) in intubated patients during a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT).

Weaning from mechanical ventilation can be difficult, especially in patients at higher risk of failure. During an SBT, losing positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) can cause the lungs to lose volume and make breathing harder by increasing the work of breathing (WOB). HFTO may help reduce the work of breathing, but previous studies using flows of 30-60 L/min did not consistently show an increase in EELV. Higher flows may create more airway pressure.

Therefore, the main question this study is trying to answer is: In intubated patients during an SBT, does HFTO at flows greater than 60 L/min increase EELV? The hypothesis is that HFTO at flows above 60 L/min will increase EELV during the SBT.

brief_summary:
Chronic diseases are the leading causes of death and disability in the US, accounting for the majority of health care spending. Among adults with chronic illnesses like hypertension, diabetes, or HIV, adherence to daily oral medications is essential but often below 50%. Why do medication adherence and preventive health service engagement remain stubbornly low? Scarcity theory offers a novel explanation in the context of poverty. It posits that economic hardship imposes a cognitive burden that shifts attention from long-term goals to immediate needs, reduces future orientation (the relative value placed on immediate vs. future outcomes), and limits mental bandwidth (the cognitive resources needed for decisions), thus undermining behaviors like daily medication adherence and service engagement. To address these gaps, our objective is to rigorously test whether and how economic scarcity affects medication adherence and preventive service uptake among older adults with chronic disease, leveraging the naturally occurring monthly fluctuation in scarcity created by the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefit cycle as a natural experiment.

There are three aims:

1. We will measure daily medication adherence objectively for four months with wireless electronic pill bottle caps (CleverCaps). We will test whether, when, and by how much adherence changes as scarcity fluctuates during the SNAP benefit cycle.
2. We will conduct two easily implementable RCTs to test whether scarcity affects participants' engagement with beneficial services requiring navigation of administrative burdens. In one trial, participants will be randomized to receive an invitation during either a high- or low- scarcity period (i.e., before vs. after SNAP receipt) to a personalized preventive health review that identifies gaps in US Preventive Services Task Force Grade A/B recommendations.25 In the second, participants will be invited to free financial counseling provided by the City of Philadelphia during a high- or low-scarcity period. We hypothesize invitation response rates will be \>15% higher during low-scarcity periods.
3. We will examine potential mechanisms that link scarcity with health behaviors by randomizing timing of validated measures of mental bandwidth and future orientation during a period of high- or low-scarcity (i.e., before vs. after SNAP receipt). Our hypothesis is that we will find differences in several measures between participants who are randomly assessed during high- vs. low-scarcity periods (i.e. before vs. after SNAP receipt).

Impact: Demonstrating that scarcity helps to explain low medication adherence and beneficial health-related service uptake can inform patient-centered adherence interventions, clinical care-delivery approaches, health-system strategies, and public health approaches to improve these health behaviors and promote healthy aging.

Financial counseling invitation early in the SNAP cycle
Aim 3 follow-up call early in the SNAP period
Preventative health review invitation late in SNAP cycle
Financial counseling invitation late in the SNAP cycle
Aim 3 follow-up call late in the SNAP cycle

Response to preventative health screening invitation
Response to financial counseling invitation

Mental bandwidth: BTACT Backward Digit Span
