brief_summary:
A tracheostomy is a surgical opening made in the windpipe (trachea) through the neck to help a person breathe. A tube is placed in the opening to keep it open. As a result, the air reaching the lungs can be cooler, drier and less well filtered. This can lead to thicker mucus, coughing, difficulty clearing secretions, and an increased risk of chest infections or breathing problems caused by mucus blockages. To help replace some of the moisture normally provided by the nose and throat, humidification is often used. Different methods of humidification are used in clinical practice, although approaches may vary between healthcare centres.

Although Heat and Moisture Exchangers (HMEs) have been available for many years for people with a tracheostomy who breathe independently, their use remains limited and varies across healthcare settings. Existing research suggests that HMEs are generally well tolerated and may help keep airway secretions thinner and easier to clear, however the evidence available is limited and further research is needed for a better understanding of the clinical benefits and limitations.

The purpose of this study is to compare two humidification methods used for tracheostomy patients receiving ventilator support in critical care: the TrachPhone, a single use Heat and Moisture Exchanger (HME) device and warm air ventilation humidification. The investigators want to understand whether either method offers advantages in secretion management, patient safety, comfort, and clinical outcomes.
primary_outcomes: feasibility and tolerability of TrachPhone
title: Trachphone vs Warm Air Humidification for Acute Trache Patients on ICU

brief_summary:
KEY INFORMATION: The purpose of this study is to understand how insulin resistance (how your body processes sugar) and PTSD might be related. The goal is to improve the health of Veterans in three ways:

1. Understanding health risks: The investigators want to learn why Veterans with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) are more likely to develop medical problems related to insulin resistance, such as diabetes.
2. Testing effects of a medication: The investigators are testing whether prazosin, a medication that studies have shown may address some PTSD symptoms, can also improve how the body responds to insulin. If it does, this could point to a specific biological pathway that could be targeted for development of new treatments to prevent insulin resistance and diabetes in Veterans with PTSD.
3. Links to depression. The investigators will also look at whether insulin sensitivity affects depression symptoms in people with PTSD. This may inform future research into treatments for PTSD.
lead_sponsor: VA Office of Research and Development
primary_outcomes: Aim 1 primary outcome
Aim 2 primary outcome
title: Assessing Trauma-related Links Between Affective and Metabolic Systems

brief_summary: The study compares treatment strategies for treatment of pleural empyema (infected fluid in the chest). It will compare standard of care antibiotic course, 2-6 weeks, to a shorter course of antibiotics, 7 days. This course is started once patients achieve adequate source control/drainage of the infected fluid collection. All other treatments and interventions in patients such as blood work, imaging, vitals, and surgery/procedures follows current standard of care and are not experimental.
primary_outcomes: empyema recurrence
title: Evaluating Antibiotic Course Upon Adequate Treatment of Empyema

brief_summary:
The primary goal of this RCT is to evaluate the effect of adding plyometric training after 12 weeks of standard intervention in patients aged 18-40 years who have undergone ACLR surgery.

The primary question to answer is does adding plyometrics training to the standard rehabilitation program has superior effect in the improvement of muscular strength, dynamic balance and functional performance in ACLR patients. Participants will be divided into two groups. Group 1 receives standard program for 18 weeks, and Group 2 receives the same standard program for 18 months, but adding the plyometrics training at week 12.
primary_outcomes: Isokinetic Quadriceps Peak Torques Normalized to Body Weight
title: The Effect of Plyometric Training in Post-ACLR Surgery

brief_summary: Postoperative pain following cesarean section remains a major clinical challenge that can impair early maternal recovery, delay ambulation, and interfere with newborn care. Photobiomodulation (PBM) is a non-invasive light therapy that uses red and near-infrared light to reduce inflammation, stimulate cellular energy (ATP) production, and promote tissue repair. The purpose of this randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of portable photobiomodulation using the MitoQUAD® device as an adjunct to standard multimodal analgesia in postpartum women undergoing cesarean section. Participants (N=210) will be randomized (1:1) to receive either active PBM or a sham device in three 15-minute sessions (at 30 minutes, 24 hours, and 36-48 hours post-cesarean). Pain intensity, rescue analgesic use, wound healing, time to ambulation, maternal satisfaction, and adverse events will be monitored over 48 hours.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity at rest at 24 Hours
title: Efficacy and Safety of Photobiomodulation for Postoperative Pain After Cesarean Section

brief_summary:
This observational case-control study will investigate whether periodontal infection and inflammation are associated with missed abortion in pregnancies without detected major fetal chromosomal abnormalities.

A total of 160 pregnant women aged 18 to 40 years and at 20 weeks of gestation or earlier are planned to be enrolled. The study will include 80 women diagnosed with missed abortion and 80 women with an ongoing uncomplicated pregnancy matched according to age and gestational week.

Participants will undergo a clinical periodontal examination, and unstimulated saliva samples will be collected. Saliva will be analyzed for selected periodontal bacteria, including Porphyromonas gingivalis, Fusobacterium nucleatum, and Tannerella forsythia, as well as inflammatory biomarkers.

Serum obtained from blood samples already collected as part of routine obstetric care will be used to measure inflammatory biomarkers, including IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, CRP, MMP-8, and prostaglandin E2. No additional blood sample will be collected solely for this study. Routine complete blood count results will also be used to calculate systemic inflammatory indices.

For participants with missed abortion, study samples and periodontal assessments will be obtained after the diagnosis has been confirmed and before uterine evacuation or medical treatment. Routine fetal genetic test results will be reviewed, and cases with detected chromosomal abnormalities included in the clinical genetic assessment will be excluded from the main analysis.

The study aims to determine whether periodontal pathogen burden, periodontal disease, and local and systemic inflammatory responses differ between women with missed abortion and women with ongoing uncomplicated pregnancies.
primary_outcomes: Salivary Porphyromonas gingivalis Burden
Salivary Fusobacterium nucleatum Burden
Salivary Tannerella forsythia Burden
title: Periodontal Pathogens and Inflammatory Biomarkers in Missed Abortion

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of denifanstat compared with matching placebo in participants with moderate to severe acne vulgaris who are ≥12 years of age. After the 12-week treatment phase, a subset of approximately 530 participants will have the option to consent to an open-label extension phase for an additional 40 weeks of treatment.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving EGSS success, defined as a score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) with at least a 2-point decrease from their baseline score
Absolute change from baseline in inflammatory lesion count (ILC)
Absolute change from baseline in non-inflammatory lesion count (ILC)
title: Phase 3 Study of Denifanstat in Participants With Moderate to Severe Acne

brief_summary: Chemotherapy combined with PD-1 inhibitor immunotherapy is the standard treatment for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), yet patient prognosis remains unsatisfactory, with a median PFS of only about 6 months and a 1-year PFS rate of only 25%. Adding anlotinib maintenance therapy on top of PD-1 inhibitor immunotherapy maintenance after chemoimmunotherapy may improve progression-free survival and overall survival. We plan to conduct a randomized, multicenter, open-label Phase II study of anlotinib combined with PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy versus PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy maintenance in advanced ESCC. A total of 112 patients with unresectable locally advanced, recurrent, or metastatic ESCC are planned to be enrolled. After enrollment, patients will receive either anlotinib combined with PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy or PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy maintenance, with a maximum treatment duration of 2 years. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of anlotinib combined with PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy in advanced ESCC by comparing it with the PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy maintenance group, further optimizing the comprehensive treatment model for esophageal cancer.
primary_outcomes: Progression-free survival
title: A Phase II Study of Anlotinib + PD-1 Inhibitor vs. PD-1 Inhibitor Maintenance After First-Line Chemoimmunotherapy in Advanced ESCC (Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma)

brief_summary: Chronic myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are hematologic disorders of the myeloid lineage characterized by clonal proliferation of hematopoietic stem cells, high risk of thrombotic-hemorrhagic complications, and transformation into secondary acute myeloid leukemia. MPNs include: myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera, and essential thrombocythemia. The low incidence, comparable to that of rare diseases, induces the in-depth study of patients and thus the need to develop a project with databases to collect clinical, biological, and therapeutic information.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda, Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico
primary_outcomes: Overall Survival
title: MPNdpoint. Single-center, Retrospective, Prospective Study of the Outcome of Patients With Philadelphia-negative Chronic Myeloproliferative Neoplasms

brief_summary: Accurate and objective assessment of clinical competencies is essential in nursing education to ensure that students acquire professional skills and contribute to the quality of patient care. The Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) is widely used to assess students' clinical skills and attitudes; however, factors such as time pressure, fear of making mistakes, direct observation by examiners, and unfamiliarity with the examination format may cause considerable examination anxiety and stress. High levels of anxiety may negatively affect students' attention, cognitive functioning, and ability to demonstrate their actual clinical competencies. Although various interventions have been investigated to reduce examination anxiety, evidence regarding the use of virtual reality (VR)-supported relaxation before OSCEs in nursing students remains limited. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the effect of a brief VR-supported relaxation experience administered before an OSCE on nursing students' examination anxiety, academic performance, and self-efficacy.
primary_outcomes: Change from anxiety, self-efficacy level,academic performance before clinical examination
Anxiety
title: Virtual Reality-Supported Relaxation Before Objective Structured Clinical Examination

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational pilot study is to assess the safety, efficacy, and tolerability of oral low dose naltrexone (LDN) in the treatment of vulvodynia. The aims it will address are:

Aim 1:To assess the efficacy of LDN by reviewing patient-reported Global Treatment Improvement scale scores after the 4-week treatment period.

Aim 2: To identify the impact on overall and vulvar pain by calculating the difference between average pre- and post-treatment PGIC, NRS, CSI and VPAQ scores.

Aim 3: To identify adverse effects that patients may experience during treatment to better understand the safety profile of this medication.

Participants will \[describe the main tasks participants will be asked to do, interventions they'll be given and use bullets if it is more than 2 items\]

* Attend a baseline clinic visit and complete PGIC, NRS, VPAQ, and CSI questionnaires
* Take 4.5 mg LDN once daily for 4 weeks
* Discontinue LDN and contact the health care team immediately in the event of adverse effects
* Attend a follow up appointment 4 weeks after medication initiation
primary_outcomes: PGIC
title: A Pilot Study on the Efficacy of Oral Low Dose Naltrexone for Vulvodynia

brief_summary:
This is a 12-month, randomized, examiner-blinded, controlled, two-arm, parallel-group, single-site clinical trial comparing a biocompatible tissue graft (Augmented Gingival Matrix barrier) with a free gingival graft (FGG) to increase the keratinized tissue around implants in medically healthy subjects. Subjects will be enrolled in a balanced manner (1:1; treatment:control) into one of the 2 following treatment arms for keratinized tissue augmentation:

1. Group A: Augmented Gingival Matrix barrier (Test group)
2. Group B: Free gingival graft (Control Group)
conditions: Keratinized Tissue Augmentation Around Dental Implants
primary_outcomes: Change in keratinized tissue width
title: Keratinized Tissue Augmentation Using Augmented Gingival Matrix Compared to Free Gingival Graft Around Implants

brief_summary: Extreme heat exposure is an escalating global public health concern, with climate change driving increases in the frequency, duration, and intensity of heat events. Projections indicate substantial increases in heat-related morbidity and mortality in the coming decades, including among children and youth, who are increasingly recognized as a physiologically vulnerable population. The purpose of this project is to evaluate the effectiveness of commonly used heat-mitigation strategies, specifically midday access daylong electric fan use, in reducing physiological strain and maintaining cognitive function, perceptual comfort, and psychological well-being in children and youth exposed to prolonged indoor heat. The study also aims to determine whether these strategies provide comparable protection in children and youth relative to young adults. Participants will complete four sessions under the same environmental conditions (31°C and 36°C), with each temperature completed twice: once with continuous electric fan use and once without fan use. The four sessions therefore consist of: (1) 31°C without fan use; (2) 31°C with fan use; (3) 36°C without fan use; and (4) 36°C with fan use.
interventions: Simulated exposure to indoor overheating without fans
Simulated exposure to indoor overheating with fans
primary_outcomes: Core temperature (Peak) during daylong exposure to indoor overheating
title: Efficacy of Electric Fans in Children During Heat Waves

brief_summary: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of a population pharmacokinetics (PK)-guided targeted ATG dosing strategy in haploidentical stem cell transplantation and to observe the GVHD-free, relapse-free survival (GRFS) in the cohort receiving this strategy.
primary_outcomes: 1-year GVHD-free and relapse-free survival rate(1-year-GRFS)
title: RCT of Population PK-guided ATG Dosing in Haplo-HSCT

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether using a soft perineal protection device (BabySlide®) in addition to standard manual perineal support during vaginal delivery can reduce the risk of perineal trauma in first-time mothers. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the use of BabySlide® reduce the risk of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI)? Does the use of BabySlide® reduce the risk of second-, third-, or fourth-degree perineal tears and/or episiotomy?

Researchers will compare women randomized to receive BabySlide® in addition to standard manual perineal support with women receiving standard manual perineal support alone to determine whether the device reduces perineal trauma during vaginal delivery.

Participants will:

be randomized during the late second stage of labour to either BabySlide® plus standard manual perineal support or standard manual perineal support alone; receive the allocated perineal protection method during vaginal delivery; have perineal outcomes assessed and documented after delivery; and complete follow-up assessments and questionnaires after delivery to evaluate recovery and pelvic floor symptoms.
conditions: Sexual Dysfunction and the Mode of Deliveries
primary_outcomes: Number of patients with OASI
title: Perineal Protection Device for Reducing Perineal Trauma During Vaginal Delivery in First-time Mothers: a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: Children engage in low amounts of activity, which predisposes them to develop health disparities as they age. Fathers may be instrumental in helping to promote physical activity in their children. The current proposal is designed to use community-engaged research methods to develop a physical activity intervention for children in which their fathers are the agents of change, and to determine the feasibility of implementing this intervention.
primary_outcomes: Attendance: The percent of the total number of participants who attend each group session.
The percent of participants who are enrolled at study completion
Satisfaction with the program as measured by the Program Satisfaction scale
title: Fathers and Children Exercising Together

brief_summary: Functional Neurological Symptom Disorders (FNSD) are one of the commonest reasons why patients are referred to neurologists. They are as disabling as neurological disorders causing similar symptoms related to more readily demonstrable pathophysiological or structural changes, however, FNSD are more commonly associated with psychiatric comorbidities. Psychotherapy is a treatment option for FNSD although there is still a dearth of reliable evidence that psychotherapy works for FNSD or how it may help. This is partly due to the nature of psychotherapeutic interventions but also to the difficulties associated with studying treatment outcome in a patient population that is highly heterogeneous in terms of aetiology and clinical presentation. This study contributes to a larger research project that is examining the efficacy of specialist psychotherapy for patients with FNSD utilising a range of approaches including objective cognitive and behavioural measures and subsequently exploring the reliability and usefulness of different outcome measurement approaches in this patient group. This study specifically aims to assess whether psychotherapy treatment in FNSD infers any change in cognitive behaviours of impulsivity and biases in the processing of emotional information. FNSD patients will complete two computer-based tasks and health-related questionnaires before, immediately after and at 6-months follow up after completing psychotherapy treatment sessions to measure any treatment-associated improvements. Data collected from patients not receiving any psychotherapy and participants without FNSD will provide longitudinal and cross-sectional control data respectively.
lead_sponsor: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: Delay discounting measure to assess the rate of discounting across delays and probabilities
Negative affective priming: evaluative categorisation task
title: Measuring Change in Individuals With Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder

brief_summary:
This study will examine how the amount of remimazolam predicted to reach its site of action relates to the depth of sedation during lower extremity surgery under spinal anesthesia. Remimazolam is a sedative used to help patients relax and feel sleepy during surgery. People may respond differently to the same amount of this medicine, and age may explain some of these differences.

Sixty adults will be enrolled at Seoul National University Hospital, with 20 participants in each age group: 19-49 years, 50-69 years, and 70 years or older. All participants will receive remimazolam using the same stepwise dose-adjustment rules. The dose will be adjusted according to repeated assessments of responsiveness. Researchers will record sedation scores, medication delivery, brain-wave signals, vital signs, recovery, and side effects.

After surgery, a computer model will estimate the remimazolam concentration at its site of action. These estimates will not be available to the clinical team during surgery. The main goal is to measure how much the concentration associated with the target level of sedation varies between patients. The study will also examine the effect of age and whether early responses can help predict an individual patient's later response.
conditions: Sedation During Lower Extremity Surgery Under Spinal Anesthesia
primary_outcomes: Between-Patient Coefficient of Variation in Model-Predicted Effect-Site Concentration Associated With Target Sedation
title: Remimazolam Concentration and Sedation Depth During Lower Extremity Surgery Under Spinal Anesthesia

brief_summary:
Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) is an immune-related inflammatory disease of the pancreas. Relapse can occur after treatment, and long-term treatment with glucocorticoids and conventional immunosuppressants can cause significant side effects.

This multicenter, single-arm, open-label study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of inebilizumab in patients with AIP. Inebilizumab targets CD19 and reduces B cells, including plasmablasts.

The study plans to enroll 50 patients with confirmed AIP, including both newly diagnosed patients and patients with relapsing disease. All eligible participants will receive inebilizumab and follow a standardized glucocorticoid dose-reduction regimen.

The primary objective is to assess whether inebilizumab can reduce the relapse rate within 32 weeks. Secondary objectives are to assess its effects on glucocorticoid use, serum IgG4 levels, B-cell counts, and other immune cells.

Peripheral blood samples and lymph node samples will be collected for exploratory mechanistic analyses to characterize circulating and tissue immune-cell populations and blood-based biomarkers during treatment and follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Recurrence rate within 6 months
title: Inebilizumab for the Treatment of Patients With Type 1 Autoimmune Pancreatitis

brief_summary: This phase II MyeloMATCH treatment trial compares the combination of azacitidine, venetoclax and quizartinib to the standard treatment of cytarabine, daunorubicin and quizartinib for the treatment of patients with FLT3-ITD mutant acute myeloid leukemia. Azacitidine and quizartinib may stop the growth of cancer cells by blocking some of the enzymes needed for cell growth. Venetoclax is in a class of medications called B-cell lymphoma-2 (BCL-2) inhibitors. It may stop the growth of cancer cells by blocking BCL-2, a protein needed for cancer cell survival. Chemotherapy drugs, such as cytarabine and daunorubicin, work in different ways to stop the growth of cancer cells, either by killing the cells, by stopping them from dividing, or by stopping them from spreading. Giving azacitidine, venetoclax and quizartinib may be more effective than giving cytarabine, daunorubicin and quizartinib for the treatment of patients with FLT3-ITD mutant acute myeloid leukemia.
primary_outcomes: Rate of measurable residual disease (MRD) negative complete response (CR)
title: Testing the Investigational Medication Combination of Azacitidine, Venetoclax, and Quizartinib Compared to the Usual Treatment of Cytarabine, Daunorubicin, and Quizartinib for Patients With FLT3-ITD Mutant Acute Myeloid Leukemia (A MyeloMATCH Treatment Trial)

brief_summary:
Losing a loved one is a difficult experience. Some people may require psychological support, but even for those who do not, grief can often feel overwhelming. Many bereaved adults report there not being enough support that is easily available for them. Some researchers have suggested that online interventions, such as phone applications (apps) could be a good way to make support easier to access. Apps can also allow people to access support anonymously. Apps can also help by prompting people to practice different skills. This means that they can test them out in their real life and learn how to best integrate them. This type of app might be particularly helpful for grief as grief does not always stay consistent but rather changes in intensity throughout the day and year.

We have developed a grief app called Daybreak. The app was developed together with grief experts and bereaved adults. The app includes information about grief, writing exercises, short exercises, a registry of resources for grief support and a place to store memories of the deceased person. In addition, the app prompts twice daily to answer two questions about the grief and do a small exercise.

We now wish to see how well the app works. To achieve this, each participant will be randomly sorted into two groups. Both groups will have access to the app for four weeks. One group will immediately access the app for four weeks and then have a four-week waiting period (eight weeks in total), while the other group start with the waiting period and then gets access to the app for four weeks (also eight weeks). We will also measure different grief-related symptoms at the beginning, middle and end of the experiment, as well as asking everyone to rate the feasibility and acceptability of the app itself. The researchers can also see how often the app was used and if people responded to the questions in the app. In the end we should be able to see if people liked the app, if they used the app regularly and if the app changed any of the grief-related difficulties.
lead_sponsor: Medical Research Council Cognition and Brain Sciences Unit
primary_outcomes: User Version of the Mobile Application Rating Scale (uMARS)
International Prolonged Grief Disorder Scale (IPGDS)
title: A Grief Support App for Adults Experiencing Bereavement

brief_summary: The primary purpose of this study is to assess the safety and tolerability of TX002100 in participants with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT). The study will also look at whether TX002100 reduces the need for blood or iron treatments, and whether it improves blood counts, such as hemoglobin levels.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of adverse events (AEs), including serious adverse events (SAEs)
Incidence of clinically significant changes from baseline in safety laboratory assessments and other safety assessments
title: Phase 1b Study of TX002100 in Participants With Hematologic Support-Dependent Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT)

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the effects of a plant extract-based dietary supplement on menopausal symptoms and health indicators in women with late perimenopause or early postmenopause.

Approximately 120 women aged 42 to 60 years will be randomly assigned to receive either the dietary supplement or a placebo daily for 12 weeks. Neither the participants nor the research team will know the assigned treatment during the study.

Assessments will include the frequency and severity of hot flashes and night sweats, menopausal symptoms, quality of life, sleep quality, emotional well-being, body composition, and selected laboratory parameters.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) Total Score
Change From Baseline in Menopause-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MENQOL) Domain Scores
title: Effects of a Dietary Supplement in Women With Late Perimenopause or Early Postmenopause

brief_summary:
This retrospective monocentric observational study aims to evaluate whether basal luteinizing hormone (LH) levels can reliably diagnose central precocious puberty and reduce the need for LHRH stimulation testing. Currently, all patients with suspected precocious puberty undergo LHRH testing regardless of basal LH levels.

The study will analyze pediatric patients evaluated between 2019 and 2024 to determine an optimal basal LH threshold with high specificity. Secondary analyses will assess diagnostic performance and explore clinical and biological factors influencing LH levels. The results may help reduce unnecessary testing and improve diagnostic strategies.
primary_outcomes: Basal LH threshold for diagnosis of central precocious puberty
title: Basal LH Threshold for the Diagnosis of Central Precocious Puberty

brief_summary: Coronary artery disease, caused by the furring up of the heart arteries by atherosclerosis, is a major cause of death in the UK. Despite existing therapies, adverse cardiovascular events remains high, especially in patients who have already had a heart attack, as some of these patients have aggressive atherosclerotic disease. If we could identify these vulnerable patients, then in wider clinical practice in the future we might be able to treat them better with new therapies that can otherwise be expensive or come with a risk of side-effects. Traditionally, the assessment of atherosclerotic disease and the identification of the plaques that will cause heart attacks is performed using invasive imaging - imaging taken by passing a wire into the arteries of the heart that has a camera on its tip. Invasive imaging, however, can be used only in patients with symptoms and has risks. Photon counting (PC) CT is a new CT system that has image quality comparable to invasive imaging and can be used in the community to examine individuals with stable angina symptoms. In this study we aim to compare how well PC-CT detects high-risk plaques compared with invasive imaging and in due course develop a platform that will expedite the analysis of CT images to allow its broad use in the clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Compare the efficacy of PC-CTA and of conventional CTA in assessing the percent atheroma volume (PAV) using the output of the NIRS-IVUS analysis as the reference standard
title: Identification of Lesion Characteristics in Coronary Plaques Using Multimodality Intravascular Imaging and Novel Photon-counting CT in Stable Angina

brief_summary: Phase 1/2 clinical trial is to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of escalating doses of IDP-121 combined with chemotherapy in patients with advanced unresectable/metastatic SCLC that have progressed after 1st line platinum- based chemotherapy, considering the role of MYC amplification in the development of platinum resistance.
primary_outcomes: MTD and RP2D
title: Phase 1/2 Multicenter, Open-label, Dose-escalation Study of IDP- 121 in Patients With Platinum-resistant Small Cell Lung Cancer (MYCrocytic)

brief_summary: purpose: to evaluate the postoperative pain incidence and intensity after three different obturation techniques (Cold lateral condensation technique (CLC), Vibration thermo-dynamic technique (Vibra-Tho) and Injection of thermo-plasticized gutta-percha (Fast Fill device)). Materials and Methods: Thirty patients with non-vital mature maxillary incisors requiring endodontic treatment will be randomly divided into three groups (n=10) according to the obturation technique used: Group I (CLC), Group II (Vibra-Tho) and Group III (Fast Fill device). Postoperative pain levels will be recorded using the visual Analogue Scale (VAS) immediately post operative and at 24 hours, 72 hours, one week and two weeks.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative pain
title: Assessment of Postoperative Pain Following Root Canal Obturation of Permanent Mature Teeth Using Three Different Obturation Techniques: A Randomized Clinical Trial

brief_summary:
Pulse oximeter probes are used to continuously monitor oxygen levels in newborn babies in intensive care. These probes are usually attached to the baby's hand or foot with adhesive tape and must be moved to a new site every few hours. Repeatedly sticking and removing adhesive can damage the delicate skin of premature babies.

The investigators have developed a new way to secure the probe without any adhesive touching the skin: the probe's adhesive side is attached to a soft, self-adhering (cohesive) bandage that wraps around the baby's hand or foot. The bandage sticks only to itself, not to the skin.

The purpose of this study is to find out whether securing the probe with a cohesive bandage protects the skin better than the standard method of taping the probe directly to the skin. Sixty-four premature babies (born at 32 to 36 weeks) will be randomly placed in one of two groups. In both groups, the probe will be placed on each hand and foot for four hours in turn, for a total of 16 hours. The skin under the probe will be photographed and scored by two nurses who do not know which method was used.
interventions: Cohesive bandage fixation of pulse oximeter probe
Standard adhesive fixation of pulse oximeter probe
primary_outcomes: Neonatal Skin Condition Score (NSCS) total score at the probe application site
title: Cohesive Bandage Fixation of Pulse Oximeter Probes and Skin Condition in Preterm Neonates

brief_summary: This interventional study evaluated physiological, molecular, and performance adaptations to different high-intensity training modalities in national-level kayak athletes. Thirty-two athletes were allocated to four parallel groups: high-intensity interval training (HIIT), sprint interval training (SIT), combined training (COMB), or a control condition (CON). The study protocol included a six-week detraining period before baseline (PRE) assessments, followed by a six-week training intervention and a subsequent six-week detraining period. Physiological assessments and blood sampling were performed at PRE and immediately after the training intervention (POST) to evaluate training-related changes. Sprint kayak performance over 500 m was assessed at PRE and POST, with additional assessments conducted 15 and 30 days after completion of the subsequent six-week detraining period. The study aimed to examine the effects of different training modalities on physiological responses, circulating molecular markers, and 500-m kayak performance, as well as changes in performance following detraining.

500-m kayak performance
Change in power output at VO₂max (POVO₂max)

Change in power output at 75% of VO₂max (PO75%VO₂max)
Change in blood lactate concentration
Change in maximal heart rate (HRmax)
Change in circulating interleukin-6 (IL-6)
Change in circulating vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A)

brief_summary:
This is a Phase II study is being done to determine whether a new combination of therapies is safe and effective for adults to treat Melanoma before surgery. The two therapies that will be combined in this study are nivolumab and RP2.

Nivolumab is a standard treatment for this type of cancer. Nivolumab targets and blocks a receptor called PD-1 on the surface of certain immune cells called T-cells. Blocking PD-1 may activate T-cells to find and kill cancer cells.

RP2 is a new treatment that is not yet FDA approved to treat this cancer. RP2 is a herpes simplex virus (a microscopic life form commonly known as the "cold sore virus") that has been changed in the laboratory to grow in and destroy cancer cells and to activate (turn on) the immune system to attack the cancer cells.
primary_outcomes: Major Pathologic Response Rate (MPR)
title: Neoadjuvant RP2 + Nivolumab in Patients With Melanoma

brief_summary: Researchers are looking for new treatments for pain. The goal of this trial is to learn if MK-6916 changes what happens to the midazolam and rosuvastatin in healthy participants' bodies. Researchers will compare the amount of midazolam and rosuvastatin in a participant's body over time when they are given with and without MK-6916.
primary_outcomes: Period 1: Area Under the Concentration-Time Curve From Time 0 to Infinity (AUC0-inf) of Midazolam
Period 2: AUC0-inf of Midazolam
Period 1: AUC0-inf of Rosuvastatin
Period 2: AUC0-inf of Rosuvastatin
title: A Clinical Trial of MK-6916 With Midazolam and Rosuvastatin in Healthy Participants (MK-6916-012)

brief_summary:
Acute post-amputation pain remains a significant clinical challenge in patients with combat-related lower limb injuries and may negatively affect early rehabilitation, mobility, and opioid consumption. Various regional analgesia techniques and cryoanalgesia have been proposed to improve pain control; however, evidence regarding their feasibility and clinical utility in military trauma populations remains limited.

The aim of this pilot study is to assess the feasibility of conducting a future randomized controlled trial evaluating different approaches to acute post-amputation pain management in patients with combat-related lower limb injuries.

This prospective non-randomized pilot study will enroll 36 adult patients undergoing lower limb amputation or reamputation following combat-related trauma. Participants will be allocated to one of three groups according to clinical indications and multidisciplinary team decision: continuous peripheral nerve blocks, preoperative cryoablation, or standard multimodal analgesia.

The primary outcomes will assess study feasibility, including recruitment rate, study completion rate, protocol adherence, and completeness of data collection. Secondary outcomes will include pain intensity assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), opioid consumption expressed as Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME), early mobility assessed using the Basic Amputee Mobility Score (BAMS), time to first standing and ambulation, and treatment-related complications.

Participants will be followed for 7 days after surgery, with an additional assessment at 1 month.

This three-year study aims to investigate gender differences in social frailty and evaluate the effects of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based conversational social-support intervention among older adults with chronic heart failure (CHF).

The study plans to enroll 300-500 adults aged 60 years or older from four Chang Gung Memorial Hospital branches in Taiwan.

In the first phase, researchers will assess participants' clinical characteristics, sarcopenia, physical activity, and physical, psychological, and social frailty. The study will examine gender differences and identify factors associated with social frailty.

In the second phase, 174 participants are planned to be assigned to three groups: an AI-based conversational social-support group, a community social participation group, and a control group. The AI group will engage in daily 15-30-minute app-based conversations, while the community group will be encouraged to participate in regular social activities. The control group will maintain routine activities.

The third phase will assess longer-term changes in social frailty, emotional well-being, physical activity, and health outcomes, with follow-up assessments at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after the intervention.

During the exercises, they will be safely supported to prevent falls, while a wearable device measures physical responses such as heart rate and skin conductance. After each task, participants will complete short questionnaires about their experience and mental effort. The study aims to determine which type of extended reality is preferred and how each affects physical and mental responses, supporting the development of more accessible rehabilitation approaches.

Children's dental fear will also be assessed with two child-friendly scales, and parents' own dental anxiety will be measured to see whether it is related to their child's anxiety. The study aims to find out whether VR storytelling differs from a traditional storybook in its effect on children's anxiety before dental treatment.

brief_summary:
This study will test the use of the UltraTrac™ system, a small, noninvasive device that uses electrodes on the skin and a small ultrasound sensor to provide measurements of cardiac function in a wide of subjects. UltraTrac estimates cardiac output and other hemodynamic parameters without needles or invasive procedures.

Up to 400 generally healthy volunteers, from infants to older adults, will take part in a single study visit lasting about one hour. During the visit, study staff place small adhesive electrodes on the skin and a lightweight ultrasound sensor on the neck or thigh. The device records heart-related signals while the participant is lying down, sitting, and during simple movements such as repositioning, passive leg raise, or light exercise (like walking or pedaling in place). The study evaluates how often the UltraTrac device can collect good-quality signals and how consistent the measurements are across different ages and activity levels.

There is no direct medical benefit to participants. The risks are minimal, such as mild skin irritation from adhesive electrodes. The information collected will help improve the UltraTrac system and support future regulatory review so that noninvasive cardiac monitoring may become more widely available, especially for children and other patients who are not able to undergo invasive monitoring.

brief_summary:
This is an open-label, multi-cohort, investigator-initiated clinical study designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of GI001 in adult patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (R/R B-NHL) and B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (R/R B-ALL).

GI001 is an exploratory, in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy targeting the CD19 antigen. Unlike traditional CAR-T cell therapies that require extensive in vitro cell manufacturing, GI001 is administered directly to the patient via intravenous infusion, aiming to generate CAR-T cells directly within the patient's body.

The study consists of two main phases:

* Dose-Escalation Phase: This phase will evaluate four ascending dose levels to assess safety, identify any Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs), determine the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD), and establish the Recommended Dose for Expansion (RDE). It utilizes an accelerated titration design for the initial doses, followed by a standard "3+3" dose-escalation design.
* Dose-Expansion Phase ： Once the RDE is identified, additional patients will be enrolled to further evaluate the safety, clinical efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of GI001 at the selected dose(s).

The primary focus of the study is to continuously monitor adverse events and evaluate the overall safety profile. Secondary objectives include assessing clinical response rates (such as Objective Response Rate and Complete Response Rate), survival outcomes, and the expansion levels of CAR-T cells in the peripheral blood.

brief_summary: Cervical cancer remains a major threat to women's health and wellbeing, with the burden disproportionately concentrated in low- and middle-income countries such as Nigeria, where inadequate awareness, limited access to screening, screening-related anxiety, and other structural and sociocultural barriers contribute to low screening uptake, late presentation, and preventable mortality. Despite the urgent need to improve early detection, there remains a critical gap in culturally appropriate, co-produced interventions to address the barriers that shape cervical cancer screening behaviours. The proposed study will address this gap by piloting the feasibility and acceptability of "cervical cancer Awareness education to aid Confidence and screening upTake (ACT)" a novel, low-intensity, co-produced workshop intervention for women who are not up to date or only partially up to date with recommended cervical cancer screening. Delivered over approximately two hours, ACT is designed to increase awareness of cervical cancer and its symptoms, strengthen understanding of the consequences of delayed screening and the benefits of early detection, improve knowledge of available screening pathways, address misconceptions and screening-related anxiety, and build women's confidence and motivation to engage with screening services. In addition to assessing recruitment, retention, intervention engagement, acceptability and implementation feasibility, the study will pilot the proposed outcome measures and data collection procedures to inform a future definitive evaluation. It will also generate preliminary evidence on potential intervention mechanisms, screening-related outcomes, and approaches to assessing cost-effectiveness. Collectively, the study will establish whether ACT is feasible, acceptable and sufficiently promising to progress to a larger-scale trial evaluating its effectiveness and cost-effectiveness in improving cervical cancer screening uptake among women in Nigeria.

Give a small blood sample by venipuncture (a needle in a vein of the arm) Repeat the blood draw about once a week for 3 to 6 weeks

brief_summary:

In Italy, approximately 300,000 individuals are affected by T1D, with a prevalence of 0.5% in the general population and 0.22% in the pediatric population. The annual incidence among children is 12.26 per 100,000, with boys affected more frequently than girls (13.13 vs. 11.35 per 100,000). Alarmingly, 25-40% of pediatric patients present with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) at disease onset. International prospective studies, such as the Environmental Determinants of Diabetes in the Young (TEDDY) study, have demonstrated that symptoms are poor predictors of CD autoimmunity, emphasizing the need for structured population-based screening strategies. Similarly, in T1D, the appearance of disease-specific autoantibodies-such as anti-GAD, insulin autoantibodies (IAA), IA-2A, and ZnT8A-can precede the onset of clinical disease by years. Identifying these markers enables early risk stratification, timely monitoring, and potential enrollment in immunomodulatory prevention trials, including those organized by TrialNet.

In this context, an observational study is being conducted at the Pediatric Department of the University of Bari. It involves the prospective screening of children (ages 1 to 18 years) with a confirmed diagnosis of celiac disease for T1D-associated autoantibodies. The study aims to enroll 600 CD patients over one year, with an anticipated 80% participation rate among eligible families.

However, ASA-PS does not directly measure nutritional depletion or muscle weakness, which are critical risk factors in geriatric patients.

The Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) is a simple, objective screening tool calculated from preoperative serum albumin levels and body weight.

The purpose of this observational study is to evaluate the role of GNRI in predicting postoperative pulmonary complications and to determine whether adding GNRI to the standard ASA-PS classification improves the ability to identify older patients at high risk for lung complications after major abdominal surgery.

brief_summary:
Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a disorder that occurs between the ages of 10 and 18, with an unknown etiology, and is characterized by a three-dimensional deformity of the spine. It is often asymptomatic at onset but may progressively lead to cosmetic and functional impairments over time. The Rigo classification, which evaluates the structural characteristics of scoliosis, is a three-dimensional functional classification system that takes into account the direction of the curve and the involved spinal regions

In studies conducted on individuals with AIS, a significant reduction in respiratory muscle strength (MIP-Maximum Inspiratory Pressure and MEP-Maximum Expiratory Pressure) has been observed, and this condition has been associated with thoracic rigidity and decreased physical activity . In individuals with AIS, a significant negative correlation has been reported between Cobb angle and FVC and FEV₁ values, as well as a moderate negative correlation between trunk rotation angle (ATR) and respiratory muscle strength (MIP and MEP). In light of these findings, it has been shown that as the severity of scoliosis increases, lung volumes decrease, and that scoliosis may affect respiration not only through a two-dimensional curvature angle but also through three-dimensional structural changes such as trunk rotation. Curves concentrated in the thoracic region according to the Rigo classification demonstrate more pronounced reductions in MIP and MEP values

The impact of AIS on quality of life has been evaluated, and it has been reported that individuals with AIS score lower than healthy individuals in domains such as body image, pain, mental health, and function
lead_sponsor: Istanbul Physical Medicine Rehabilitation Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: MIP,MEP,"Curve type according to the Rigo classification"
title: The Effect of Curve Type Determined According to the Rigo Classification on Respiratory Muscle Strength, Quality of Life, and Functional Status in Individuals Diagnosed With Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.

brief_summary:
Arm swelling can persist after breast cancer treatment and may interfere with comfort, movement, and everyday activities. Decongestive care combines several approaches to manage this swelling. This study examined whether adding radial shock wave treatment changed short-term outcomes compared with decongestive care alone.

Twenty-one adults with stage 2 or stage 3 lymphedema affecting one arm were assigned to two treatment groups. Both groups were allocated to a four-week decongestive program. The combined-treatment schedule also included twelve shock wave sessions. Assessments before and after treatment covered arm size, the thickness of the skin and the tissue beneath it, pain, difficulty using the arm, lymphedema-related quality of life, and shoulder and wrist movement. A physician who did not know the treatment assignment performed the physical and ultrasound measurements.
primary_outcomes: Reduction in calculated affected upper-limb volume
title: Radial Shock Wave Treatment Alongside Decongestive Care for Arm Swelling After Breast Cancer

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will investigate whether static or dynamic hand orthoses used as adjuncts to occupational therapy improve upper extremity recovery in adults with subacute stroke. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three parallel groups: conventional occupational therapy alone, occupational therapy combined with a dynamic hand orthosis, or occupational therapy combined with a static hand orthosis. All groups will receive a standardized occupational therapy program for 4 weeks. Participants in the two orthosis groups will additionally use the assigned orthosis for 120 minutes per day, 5 days per week, following the occupational therapy session. Clinical outcomes will be assessed at baseline, at the end of the 4-week intervention, and at 8 weeks from the start of the intervention. The primary outcome will be upper extremity motor function assessed with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE).
primary_outcomes: Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE)
title: Upper Extremity Orthoses Combined With Occupational Therapy in Subacute Stroke

brief_summary: This prospective study aims to compare the clinical, perioperative, and postoperative outcomes of flexible ureterorenoscopy using a direct in-scope suction system (DISS) with standard flexible ureterorenoscopy in patients undergoing retrograde intrarenal surgery for renal or proximal ureteral stones. A total of 70 patients will be enrolled, with 35 patients in each group. The study will assess postoperative infectious complications, including fever, systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), and sepsis, as well as operative parameters, length of hospital stay, reoperation, and stone-free status. Stone-free status will be assessed by non-contrast computed tomography four weeks after surgery.
interventions: Flexible ureterorenoscope with direct in-scope suction
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Postoperative Fever
title: Direct In-Scope Suction Versus Standard Flexible Ureterorenoscopy

brief_summary:
Patients with congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) have traditionally been discouraged from physical activity and competitive sports, although the rate of exercise-related arrhythmic events is considered low. In recent years, international guidelines have become less restrictive and now support shared decision-making between physicians, patients and families to promote safe physical activity. Excessive restriction, especially in young people, may negatively affect mental health, quality of life and overall cardiovascular risk. However, little is known about the physical activity level and physical fitness of patients with LQTS in clinical practice.

This observational study will describe the baseline functional capacity, physical activity level and quality of life of adults with congenital LQTS followed at the Arrhythmia Outpatient Clinic of the Heart Institute (InCor), São Paulo, Brazil, and compare them with patients with arrhythmias and a structurally normal heart. Participants will answer questionnaires on physical activity, quality of life and barriers to exercise, and will undergo cardiopulmonary exercise testing and 24-hour Holter monitoring. This is the first step of the Channelopathies Movement and Exercise Study (CANMOVE).
primary_outcomes: Peak oxygen consumption (VO2 peak)
title: Physical Activity and Functional Capacity in Patients With Congenital Long QT Syndrome

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled online experiment will test whether adding an ultra-processed food (UPF) warning label or a positive not-ultra-processed (Not-UPF) label, to the FDA's proposed Nutrition Information Box (NIB) changes consumer perceptions of UPFs among U.S. adults.

Participants will be randomized to one of four label conditions and will evaluate UPF and Not-UPF products with different nutritional profiles of 3 food categories: yogurts, cereals, and sliced breads. The primary outcome is shelf choice and the secondary outcomes are correct identification of UPF products, perceived healthfulness, perceived usefulness, and perceived message effectiveness.

This experiment aims to answer the following questions:

Do UPF warning labels and Not-UPF labels shift shelf choice toward Not-UPF products compared to the NIB alone? Is a UPF warning label more effective than a Not-UPF label at shifting shelf choice, decreasing perceived healthfulness, improving correct identification of UPFs, and increasing perceived usefulness and perceived message effectiveness?

Researchers will compare outcomes across the four randomized arms to estimate the independent effect of adding a UPF warning label versus a Not-UPF label beyond nutrient disclosure in the NIB alone.
interventions: NIB: Label exposure in mock-up UPF and Not-UPF products
NIB+UPFWL: Label exposure in mock-up UPF and Not-UPF products
NIB+Not-UPF Black: Label exposure in mock-up UPF and Not-UPF products
NIB+Not-UPF Green: Label exposure in mock-up UPF and Not-UPF products
lead_sponsor: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
primary_outcomes: Shelf Choice (UPF or Not UPF product)
title: Testing Ultra-processed Warning Labels and Not-Ultra-processed Labels in United States

brief_summary: The aim of this project is to examine whether flavonoids, which are small molecules naturally present in cocoa, as well as fruits and vegetables such as berries, tea, citrus fruits, apple (typically responsible for giving these foods their strong colours), can be used to protect the human vascular system. Impaired vascular function, as determined by measuring vasodilator responses to various everyday stimuli, can be linked to elevated blood pressure (hypertension) and prevalence of cardiovascular disease. Vascular response to mental stress in particular have been shown to be associated with future risk of cardiovascular disease. Findings from this study could have implications for effective prevention of cardiovascular events in groups with increased cardiovascular risk, such as South Asians and in particular, South Asian women.
primary_outcomes: Forearm oxygen saturation (NIRS) during mental stress (SO2)
title: Impact of Dietary Flavanols on Microvascular Function in Young Females During Mental Stress

brief_summary: Individuals with overweight experience chronic, pervasive stigma, which is a significant contributor to poor health outcomes (Puhl \& Heuer, 2010). The negative consequences of stigma are further worsened among individuals with overweight who internalize and apply stigmatizing attitudes to themselves, a process called weight self-stigma (Lillis et al., 2010). Despite its prevalence and consequences, there are notably few evidence-based interventions for weight self-stigma (Pearl \& Puhl, 2018), with acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) being the most studied treatment to-date. Previous trials have found ACT effective for addressing weight self-stigma among adults with overweight through a one-day workshop (Lillis et al., 2009) and 10-week group (Palmeira et al., 2017). A self-guided ACT intervention has potential benefits for increasing access and reach of these services, which is supported by positive results in trials evaluating ACT delivered in a self-help book (Levin et al., 2018; Potts et al., 2022) and a digital intervention format (Levin et al., 2021). However, these self-guided interventions included weight self-stigma as a more secondary focus and no studies have evaluated a digital ACT intervention designed specifically to address weight self-stigma. The proposed RCT will evaluate a digital ACT single session intervention relative to a waitlist control in a sample of 100 adults reporting overweight and high weight self-stigma.
primary_outcomes: Weight Self-Stigma Questionnaire
title: Digital Acceptance & Commitment Therapy for Weight Self-stigma

brief_summary:
Background:

Digital Smile Design (DSD) has become an important component of contemporary esthetic dentistry, allowing clinicians to visualize proposed treatment outcomes and improve communication with patients and dental technicians. Conventional computer-aided design (CAD) workflows, such as Exocad, provide individualized designs but require considerable operator expertise and time and may be influenced by operator-related variability. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted CAD systems have recently been introduced to automate parts of the design process and potentially improve efficiency, consistency, and esthetic predictability. However, direct clinical comparisons between AI-assisted and conventional CAD workflows for laminate veneer smile design remain limited.

Aim:

This prospective randomized crossover study aims to compare AI-assisted and conventional manual CAD workflows for digital smile design in patients indicated for maxillary anterior laminate veneers, focusing on patient-reported satisfaction, esthetic and functional design outcomes, and software efficiency.

Methods:

A total of 44 adult participants indicated for laminate veneer treatment were recruited from the Oral and Dental Diagnostic Center, Faculty of Dentistry, King Salman International University. The sample size includes allowance for an anticipated 20% attrition. Participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two crossover sequences: AI-assisted CAD followed by conventional CAD, or conventional CAD followed by AI-assisted CAD. A washout period of at least 48 hours will separate the two mock-up evaluations.

Standardized DSD photographs and intraoral scans will be obtained for each participant. Two digital smile designs will then be produced: one using AI-assisted software and the other using the conventional manual Exocad Smile Creator workflow. Both designs for each case will be completed under standardized conditions to minimize operator-related variability. The resulting virtual designs will be 3D printed to fabricate silicone indices for intraoral mock-up trials. Participants will evaluate both mock-ups while remaining blinded to the design method.

Outcomes:

The primary outcome will be patient esthetic satisfaction with each mock-up, assessed using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS; 0-10). Secondary outcomes will include objective design-based esthetic parameters, including facial landmark and plane accuracy, tooth proportions, symmetry, gingival zenith symmetry, incisal edge position, midline alignment, and contour accuracy. Functional outcomes will include occlusal contacts, incisal guidance, and interproximal contact length. Software efficiency will also be assessed through design time and operator-rated ease of use. Three blinded prosthodontists will evaluate the esthetic and functional characteristics of the virtual designs.

Statistical Analysis and Ethics:

Data normality will be evaluated using the Shapiro-Wilk test, followed by appropriate parametric or non-parametric statistical analyses. The protocol reviewed by the Research Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Dentistry, King Salman International University. Written informed consent obtained from all participants, and collected data will be coded, securely stored, and treated confidentially.

Expected Significance:

The study is designed to provide evidence on whether AI-assisted CAD workflows differ from conventional CAD workflows in patient satisfaction, esthetic and functional design outcomes, and workflow efficiency. By integrating patient-centered intraoral mock-up evaluation with objective virtual-model assessment in a crossover design, the study may help inform the evidence-based incorporation of AI into digital workflows for laminate veneer treatment.
interventions: mockup for laminate veneers using AI-assisted CAD software
primary_outcomes: Esthetic satisfaction for each mock up
title: AI-Assisted vs. Conventional Digital Smile Design for Laminate Veneers: A Prospective Crossover Study

brief_summary:
Neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome (NOWS) can affect a newborn infant's ability to eat, sleep, and be consoled after exposure to opioids before birth. Standard care at the participating neonatal units uses the Eat, Sleep, Console (ESC) approach, which emphasizes supportive care and involvement of parents and caregivers.

VOICE-NAS is a two-centre feasibility study evaluating whether a recorded parent/caregiver voice can be safely and practically added to usual ESC-based care for infants with NOWS. Approximately 15 to 20 infants will be enrolled at HSC Women's Hospital and St. Boniface Hospital in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

A parent or caregiver will make a short voice recording in their preferred or native language. The recording may include natural talking, reading, singing, storytelling, or comforting words. The recording will be played for the infant during clinically appropriate feeding and settling periods, usually during the latter part of a feed and/or after feeding while the infant is trying to settle or sleep. Playback will generally last about 20 minutes and will be delivered at a controlled sound level.

The main purpose of the study is to determine whether the intervention can be delivered consistently and safely within routine NICU care. The study will measure whether usable voice recordings can be obtained, how often planned playback sessions are successfully delivered, reasons sessions are missed or stopped, caregiver acceptability, staff workflow issues, and any signs of intolerance.

Clinical information such as ESC assessments, feeding support, medication treatment for NOWS, and hospital length of stay will also be described. The study is not designed to determine whether recorded voice therapy is effective. Results will be used to help design a future larger clinical trial.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Enrolled Infants With a Usable Parent/Caregiver Voice Recording Obtained
Proportion of Prescribed Voice Playback Sessions Successfully Delivered
title: Recorded Parent/Caregiver Voice for Infants With Neonatal Opioid Withdrawal Syndrome

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effect of labor dance on labor pain in primiparous women. Primiparous women admitted for vaginal birth to seven hospitals of a university affiliated private hospital group in Istanbul, Turkiye, were randomly assigned to a labor dance group or a routine care group. Women in the dance group danced to music of their choice at 30 minute intervals from 4 cm cervical dilatation until full dilatation, using movements intended to widen the pelvic diameters, in addition to routine intrapartum care. Labor pain was measured with a Visual Analogue Scale at 4 cm dilatation and repeatedly until full dilatation. Cervical dilatation and the duration of the active phase of labor were recorded.
primary_outcomes: Labor pain intensity
title: Effect of Dance on Labor Pain in Primiparous Women

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate a resident-led program designed to promote social connection among older adults living in subsidized housing communities in Baltimore. A small group of residents, called Resident Champions, will receive training and support from the research team to form a Social Connection Collective and develop activities that encourage residents to connect with one another and build peer support networks.

The study will assess whether the program is feasible and acceptable to residents and will explore whether participation is associated with changes in social isolation, social connectedness, and sense of belonging. Resident Champions will participate in approximately six group sessions over about six months, help organize community activities, and complete surveys and interviews before and after the intervention. Other residents in the housing communities may complete surveys about social connections and experiences.

brief_summary:
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and follicular lymphoma (FL) represents approximately 50% of all newly diagnosed patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. This study will assess adverse events and change in disease activity in adult Korean participants with DLBCL under routine clinical practice.

Epcoritamab is an approved drug for the treatment of DLBCL and FL. Approximately 175 adult participants who are prescribed epcoritamab by their doctors will be enrolled sites in Korea.

Participants will receive epcoritamab as prescribed by their physician. Participants will be followed for up to 24 weeks.

There is expected to be no additional burden for participants in this trial. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic according to their routine clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants with Adverse Event (AEs)
title: A Study to Assess Change in Disease State and Adverse Events in Korean Adult Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) or Follicular Lymphoma (FL) Receiving Epcoritamab Injections

brief_summary:
This study will compare opioid-free anesthesia and opioid-based anesthesia in adult euthyroid patients undergoing elective thyroidectomy. Opioid-based anesthesia is commonly used during surgery, but opioids may be associated with adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, respiratory depression, hyperalgesia, and increased postoperative opioid use. Opioid-free anesthesia uses non-opioid medications as part of a multimodal strategy to provide intraoperative analgesia.

The main aim of this prospective randomized study is to evaluate whether opioid-free anesthesia changes the perioperative oxidative stress response compared with opioid-based anesthesia. Oxidative stress will be assessed using serum biomarkers, including native thiol, total thiol, disulfide, total antioxidant status, total oxidant status, and oxidative stress index.

Eligible patients will be randomly assigned to receive either opioid-free anesthesia or fentanyl-based opioid anesthesia. Blood samples will be collected before anesthesia induction, 30 minutes after extubation, and 24 hours after surgery. The study will also compare postoperative pain scores, rescue analgesic requirement, postoperative nausea and vomiting, recovery characteristics, and intraoperative hemodynamic variables between the two anesthesia strategies.
primary_outcomes: Change in Oxidative Stress Index From Preoperative Baseline to 24 Hours After Surgery
title: Opioid-Free Versus Opioid-Based Anesthesia in Thyroid Surgery

brief_summary:
The aim of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate and compare the clinical performance of a Ni-Ti shape-memory sectional matrix system versus a conventional sectional matrix system in Class II direct composite restorations.

The study will specifically assess the following clinical parameters:

1. Proximal contact tightness
2. Proximal contour quality
3. Fracture and retention of the restoration
4. Marginal adaptation These clinical parameters will be evaluated immediately after restoration placement and after a 1-year follow-up using standardized clinical assessment methods, including the FDI criteria, dental floss evaluation, and radiographic assessment, where applicable.

Fracture and retention, and marginal adaptation will be assessed according to predefined scoring criteria.
primary_outcomes: Proximal Contact Tightness
title: Ni-Ti Shape-Memory Versus Conventional Sectional Matrices Systems in Class II Composite Restorations: A Randomized Clinical Trial

brief_summary:
Fibromyalgia (FMS) is characterized by chronic musculoskeletal pain, sleep disturbances, and fatigue. It is not entirely clear how Bcomplex vitamins affect the human pain system, while at the same time there have been approaches that use melatonin in patients with FMS and report improvements in pain and sleep quality.

The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy of a combined immunonutrition and melatonin intervention in patients with FMS through a randomized clinical trial (RCT). The combined effect of immunonutrition and melatonin, administered intravenously once a week and orally respectively, versus placebo, will be examined in patients with FMS, for a period of 5 weeks. The primary endpoints concern the quantification of pain and quality of life, while the secondary endpoints are sleep quality, fatigue and inflammatory markers.
interventions: Melatonin 1mg and intravenous B-complex vitamin drip
primary_outcomes: VAS pain

Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy (FACIT)
Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC)

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical study will compare the accuracy of immediate implant placement performed using three different surgical approaches: freehand surgery, conventional tooth-supported static computer-guided surgery, and a tooth- and socket-supported static surgical guide.

Patients requiring extraction of a mandibular first or second molar, or a retained root in the same region, followed by immediate implant placement will be enrolled. All participants will undergo three-dimensional preoperative treatment planning using cone-beam computed tomography and intraoral scanning. Participants will then be randomly allocated to one of three groups according to the assigned surgical technique.

The primary outcome will be the three-dimensional accuracy of implant placement, determined by comparing the virtually planned implant position with the clinically achieved implant position. Coronal, apical, angular, and depth deviations will be evaluated using postoperative three-dimensional imaging.

The study will determine whether the use of conventional tooth-supported or tooth- and socket-supported static surgical guides results in different implant positioning accuracy compared with freehand immediate implant placement.
interventions: Tooth- and Socket-Supported Static Guided Implant Placement
primary_outcomes: Three-dimensional implant placement accuracy

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to analyze pulmonary complications after TEVAR procedures and to identify the risk factors associated with these complications. The study population will consist of adult patients with degenerative and/or traumatic aortic disease who are candidates for TEVAR or who have undergone TEVAR between October 1, 2018, and December 31, 2025, with scheduled follow-up completion by December 2026. The aims of the study are:

* To provide information on pulmonary complications following TEVAR and their associated risk factors.
* To contribute to the planning of preventive interventions and targeted treatments to reduce pulmonary complications following TEVAR.
* To improve clinical outcomes for patients undergoing TEVAR.

Participants will be recruited retrospectively and prospectively.

This completed randomized controlled trial evaluated AI-Integrated Virtual Reality Speech Therapy (AI-IVR-ST) against conventional speech therapy in children aged 5 to 12 years with articulation and/or phonological disorders. Sixty-four children were randomized equally to two groups and received treatment three times per week for 12 weeks. The principal efficacy outcome was Percentage of Consonants Correct (PCC). Additional outcomes included GFTA-3, PPVT-4, therapy engagement and adherence, FACES III, and ASHA NOMS.

The secondary aim is to determine if IMT improves 6-minute walk test (6MWT), dyspnea, Maximal Inspiratory Pressure (MIP) pre-operatively. brief_summary: This is a two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the effectiveness of a gamified virtual reality (VR)-based exercise program in reducing suicidal ideation among community-dwelling older adults, compared with a conventional exercise control condition, and to assess the durability of effects over a 30-day follow-up period. A total of 220 eligible older adults (men and women) aged 60 years and above with clinically confirmed suicidal ideation will be randomized (1:1) to either a 5-week gamified VR-based exercise intervention or a conventional exercise control condition. Both interventions are delivered three times per week for five weeks (15 sessions total). The primary outcome is suicidal ideation severity, measured using the Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSSI) at baseline, post-intervention, and 30-day follow-up. Sex differences in intervention response will be examined as a secondary objective. This study has been approved by the Institutional Review Board of the Sports Sciences Research Center (Approval ID: IR.SSRC.REC.1404.029).

title: Gamified Virtual Reality Exercise for Suicidal Ideation in Older Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to learn how different temperature and humidity conditions affect breathing, lung function, exercise capacity, symptoms, and other physical responses in children and youth aged 11 to 18 years with asthma, compared with age- and sex-matched children and youth without asthma.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do different temperature and humidity conditions affect lung function, breathing symptoms, exercise capacity, and physiological responses in children and youth with asthma?
* Do children and youth with asthma respond differently to these environmental conditions than children and youth without asthma?
* Do sex and gender influence these responses?

Researchers will compare children and youth with asthma to age- and sex-matched children and youth without asthma to see if temperature and humidity exposures have different effects on breathing, exercise performance, symptoms, and physiological responses.

Participants will:

* Attend two study visits in a climate-controlled chamber.
* Be exposed to hot, cold, and varying humidity conditions for short periods of time.
* Complete breathing tests and exercise testing before, during, and after each exposure.
* Have symptoms, physical activity, and physiological responses monitored throughout the study.
lead_sponsor: University of Ontario Institute of Technology
primary_outcomes: Change in Lung Function as Measured by Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (FEV1)
Change in Forced Vital Capacity (FVC)
title: Testing the Effects of Temperature & Humidity on Children With and Without Asthma in an Environmental Climatic Chamber
