Access is intended from the availability of FUSION clinical trial results until commercial availability of ulefnersen in participating countries. Ulefnersen is provided free of charge.
title: Early Access Program for Ulefnersen in Children, Adolescents and Adults With FUS-associated Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (FUS-ALS)

brief_summary:
In orthodontic treatment involving extraction of the maxillary first premolars, the canine is distalized into the extraction space using sliding mechanics. Because the retraction force is applied at bracket level and therefore at a distance from the centre of resistance of the tooth, the canine tends to rotate distopalatally and to tip in the sagittal plane instead of translating bodily. These side effects lengthen treatment and increase the load on the posterior anchorage teeth.

Power arms are used to bring the line of action of the force closer to the centre of resistance. In addition, because the centre of resistance of the maxillary canine lies palatal to the mid-buccolingual axis of the crown, a force applied from the palatal surface generates a rotational moment opposite in direction to that produced by a buccal force.

This trial tested whether dividing a constant total distalizing force between the buccal and the palatal surfaces of the canine, so that the two rotational moments oppose one another, produces a more bodily canine movement than applying the whole force from the buccal side alone.

The trial used a split-mouth design: in each participant one maxillary quadrant received the whole force from the buccal side and the contralateral quadrant received half the force buccally and half palatally, with the total force identical on both sides. Canine displacement, rotation, tipping and first molar anchorage loss were measured on superimposed digital models over 12 weeks.
interventions: Combined buccal and palatal distalizing force
primary_outcomes: Cumulative maxillary canine distalization
title: Additional Palatal Force in Maxillary Canine Distalization

brief_summary:
Cardiovascular disease is a major cause of morbidity and mortality among women. Cardiovascular risk in women is influenced not only by traditional risk factors, but also by sex-specific factors and social determinants of health. However, information on the distribution and relative importance of these factors among Mexican women remains limited.

REFARCAM Mx is a multicenter, observational, cross-sectional registry designed to estimate the prevalence and describe the distribution of traditional, sex-specific, and emerging cardiovascular risk factors, as well as social determinants of health, among adult female beneficiaries of the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) receiving care at participating medical units in Mexico.

Approximately 3,000 women aged 18 years or older will be enrolled across 36 IMSS medical units representing the three levels of healthcare. Participants will complete the validated REFARCAM Mx questionnaire administered by trained personnel using a secure digital platform. Clinical and anthropometric information, including blood pressure, weight, height, and heart rate, will also be collected, and available clinical information will be verified using the institutional medical record. In women aged 40 to 74 years, cardiovascular risk will be estimated using the HEARTS for the Americas cardiovascular risk calculator.

The collected information will be used to characterize cardiovascular risk in women receiving care at participating IMSS centers and to explore factors associated with previous cardiovascular events. Statistical analyses will include conventional multivariable methods and machine-learning approaches to identify relevant patterns and predictors of cardiovascular risk.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence and Distribution of Cardiovascular Risk Factors
Factors Associated With High Cardiovascular Risk
Prevalence of Sex-Specific Cardiovascular Risk Factors
Prevalence of Social Determinants of Health
title: Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Mexican Women

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect of a nurse-led, stigma-reduction-based epilepsy education program on perceived/internalized stigma, concealment of epilepsy, and self-management among adults with epilepsy.

Participants will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group will receive a structured nurse-led education program consisting of four weekly sessions, each lasting approximately 45-60 minutes. The program will address epilepsy-related knowledge and misconceptions, stigma and self-stigma, disclosure and concealment of epilepsy, communication, medication adherence, seizure triggers, stress management, seizure diaries, and individual self-management planning. The control group will receive routine care without additional structured education during the study period.

Outcomes related to epilepsy stigma, concealment, and self-management will be assessed using validated measurement tools.
primary_outcomes: Change in Epilepsy-Related Stigma
Change in Concealment of Epilepsy
Change in Epilepsy Self-Management
title: Effects of Nurse-Led Stigma-Reduction Education in Epilepsy

brief_summary: DS-9606a demonstrates antitumor activity in patients with solid tumors known to express CLDN-6, primarily in patients with testicular GCT, with a manageable safety profile with appropriate risk minimization measures. The purpose of this Medical Access Program (MAP) is to provide access to DS-9606a to eligible patients with advanced testicular GCT who have received standard of care treatment and, in their treating physician's opinion, have an unmet clinical need and cannot enter a clinical trial.

brief_summary:
Unscheduled care is care "that does not constitute a life-threatening emergency but for which treatment by a healthcare professional is desirable within 48 hours" and 80% of general practitioners organize their schedules to provide unscheduled care each day. In Multidisciplinary Health Centers, 58% of general practitioners report that they systematically address requests for unscheduled care through a collective response to these requests.

Despite this, difficulties in accessing healthcare are worsening and according to a survey by France Asso Santé, 44% of French people report that they have already foregone healthcare due to excessively long waiting times, and in 2025, 80% reported having foregone care at least once, with 67% claiming this is due to excessively long waiting times for appointments.

The literature shows that it is linked to two main factors: precarious living conditions (financial barriers) and limited healthcare availability, which reinforce one another, as people living in poor conditions are three times more likely to forego care than others.Indeed, in areas underserved by general practitioners, this risk becomes more than eight times higher than that of the rest of the population.

Nationwide, the density of general practitioners was 153 GPs per 100,000 residents in 2012 and 140 per 100,000 in 2021; it is expected to continue declining over the next decade. GPs work work an average of 55 hours per week and, as their number is declining, it is essential to reorganize primary care services.Regarding non-emergency care, in 2019 17% of French people reported that they had sought emergency room care because no doctors were available (according to a survey by France Asso Santé). Many visits to the emergency room could be avoided because they fall under the purview of community-based care. This misuse appears to be linked to several factors, including the lack of availability of appropriate primary care and the greater financial accessibility of third-party payment, which is consistent with the factors leading to forgoing care. In Occitanie, the 2024 ORU report found that 20% of emergency department visits could potentially be handled by primary care. Changes in the organization of community health services are gradually emerging, notably thanks to task delegation and the creation of coordinated care structures but this has not been sufficient to prevent a deterioration in access to community-based care. The medical team at the La Source MSPU is well aware of this public health issue and the inequality in access to care for all. In light of this, the MSPU proposes to organize a primary care team to manage access to and coordinate unscheduled care services within the organization. This innovative structure is referred to as the Coordinated Structure for Unscheduled Care (SC-SNP). A walk-in consultation window is open every morning from Monday through Friday to address requests for unplanned care. This system mobilizes a dedicated primary care team consisting of a medical assistant, a registered nurse, and a general practitioner.
primary_outcomes: Number of consultations per hour for walk-in care BEFORE implementing the Controlled Structure for Unscheduled Care at the La Source MSPU
Number of consultations per hour for walk-in care AFTER implementing the Controlled Structure for Unscheduled Care at the La Source MSPU
title: Coordinated Primary Care Team to Access and Regulate Unscheduled Care

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether the depth of anesthesia at the moment the breathing tube is placed is related to how easily the tube can be placed, in adult women (18 to 65 years) having planned surgery under general anesthesia. Depth of anesthesia is measured with the Patient State Index (PSI), a number from 0 to 100 shown by a brain-activity monitor (SedLine) with a sensor placed on the forehead; lower numbers mean deeper anesthesia.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the PSI at the moment of tube placement related to the quality of intubation conditions: how relaxed the jaw is, how open the vocal cords are, and whether the patient coughs or moves?
* Does the PSI tell the anesthesia team something about these conditions beyond what they already know from the anesthetic dose, the timing of the muscle relaxant, and the patient's age?

There is no comparison group; all participants are in one group.

Participants will:

* Receive their usual anesthesia care. The study does not change any drug, dose or timing, and all decisions stay with their anesthesiologist.
* Have their depth of anesthesia and muscle relaxation recorded with monitors that are already part of routine care at this hospital. While the breathing tube is being placed, the brain-activity monitor screen is turned away from the anesthesiologist placing the tube, and a second doctor watches it the whole time.
* Answer a few short questions on the day after surgery about sore throat, hoarseness, and whether they remember anything from the operation.
interventions: Depth of anesthesia at laryngoscopy (Patient State Index)
primary_outcomes: Composite Intubation Condition Score
title: Patient State Index at Laryngoscopy and Tracheal Intubation Conditions

brief_summary: Complex PTSD (CPTSD) is a new diagnosis for which no established gold-standard treatment(s) yet exists. In this trial, three psychotherapies, Prolonged Exposure (PE), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), and Enhanced Skills Training in Affective and Interpersonal Regulation (ESTAIR), are compared in a multisite trial. Methods: The study is a single-blinded, pragmatic, non-inferiority, multi-center randomized controlled trial (RCT) comparing ESTAIR, EMDR vs PE for CPTSD, each delivered as 18 weekly individual sessions. In total, 315 patients will be recruited from three outpatient clinics in the Capital Region of Denmark and randomized to one of the three intervention arms. The primary outcome is patient-rated CPTSD symptoms assessed with the International Trauma Questionnaire (ITQ); secondary outcomes include clinician-rated CPTSD symptoms assessed with the International Trauma interview (ITI), as well as dissociation, quality of life, attachment, interpersonal problems, and emotion regulation. Assessments are conducted before and after therapy (18 weekly sessions) treatment and at 6-month follow-up. Weekly patient- and clinician-rated outcomes are collected at every treatment session. Outcome assessors, blind to treatment allocation, will perform the observer-based symptom ratings, while fidelity assessors will monitor manual adherence.
primary_outcomes: International Trauma Questionnaire
title: RECONNECT - Treatments for Complex PTSD

brief_summary: This study compares two 12-week conditioning programs in 48 competitive table tennis players. Players were randomly assigned to an experimental group or a control group. The experimental group followed an individualized conditioning program in which training intensity, volume, and content were adjusted weekly according to each athlete's morning heart-rate variability (HRV, 5-minute supine rMSSD) and acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR) computed from session-RPE training load. On days when HRV fell more than one standard deviation below the athlete's rolling 7-day average, high-intensity components were replaced with low-intensity work. The control group followed a standardized conditioning program matched for session frequency (three integrated sessions per week for 12 weeks, no individualized monitoring feedback). The program progressed through eight phases (foundation, accumulation, deload, intensification, transition, taper I-II, peak/post-test). Both groups were assessed before and after the intervention on 24 measures of neuromuscular performance (jump height, reactive strength index, rate of force development, force asymmetry, EMG onset latency and peak amplitude), sensorimotor performance (simple and saccadic reaction time, movement time, balance), cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max, heart-rate recovery, blood lactate), and competitive match performance (win rate, stroke accuracy, placement accuracy, rally efficiency, ball speed, national ranking points). The primary outcome is simple reaction time. The study tests whether readiness-guided individualization improves performance more than standardized conditioning. The study protocol, dataset, and analysis code are openly available in the Zenodo repository (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21343993).
lead_sponsor: The Jerzy Kukuczka Academy of Physical Education in Katowice
primary_outcomes: Simple Reaction Time
title: Individualized Physical Conditioning Based on Heart Rate Variability and Workload Monitoring in Table Tennis Players

brief_summary: Surgical intervention remains the primary treatment option for early-stage lung cancer. With the proven efficacy of immunotherapy in the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), neoadjuvant immunotherapy has increasingly become a focal point of research. Blocking vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) not only inhibits the proliferation of vascular endothelial cells and the formation of new blood vessels but also improves the tumor microenvironment and enhances the infiltration of cytotoxic T lymphocytes within it. Simultaneously targeting the VEGF and PD-L1 pathways can create a synergistic anti-cancer effect. PM8002 injection is a bispecific antibody drug that targets both PD-L1 and VEGF, functioning as a dual-action agent that combines immune suppression and anti-angiogenesis. In patients with locally advanced stage II-III NSCLC, neoadjuvant therapy that concurrently targets PD-L1/VEGF in combination with chemotherapy can improve pathological response rates, provided that the safety of the drug combination is maintained. This approach offers additional benefits to patients, prolongs event-free survival (EFS), and improves prognosis.
conditions: Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
primary_outcomes: Pathologic complete response (PCR) rate
title: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Combined With Bispecific Antibody Versus Combined With Monoclonal Antibody in Locally Advanced NSCLC

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial will compare the effects of incentive spirometer therapy with and without transcutaneous electrical diaphragmatic stimulation (TEDS) in females who have undergone mastectomy.

The study will include females aged 30 to 48 years who have undergone unilateral simple or radical mastectomy following breast cancer and are at least 3 months after surgery. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups.

Participants in one group will receive conventional physiotherapy along with transcutaneous electrical diaphragmatic stimulation and incentive spirometer training. Participants in the other group will receive conventional physiotherapy and incentive spirometer training without TEDS. Treatment will be provided over 4 weeks.

The study will evaluate changes in breathing-related symptoms, functional capacity, lung function, and quality of life. These outcomes will be assessed using a dyspnea index, Timed Up and Go test, pulmonary function testing (spirometry), and the Short Form-36 health survey. Assessments will be performed at baseline and after 4 weeks of treatment.

The study aims to determine whether adding transcutaneous electrical diaphragmatic stimulation to incentive spirometer therapy provides additional benefits for post-mastectomy females.
primary_outcomes: Pulmonary Function (FEV/FVC) Assessed by Spirometry
title: Incentive Spirometry With and Without Transcutaneous Electric Diaphragmatic Stimulation in Post-mastectomy Patients

How far does vibration affect the changes in epidermis layers in the M1? What conditions affect the most in the plantar surface, the different vibrations or the different time assessment?

Researchers will compare the three different time assessment (immediate, 20 mins delay and 30 mins delay) in two different vibrations (50 Hz and 100 Hz) to see how far the plantar skin surface changes in thickness, stiffness, and micro circulation.

1. Participants will get their M1 checked and measured by Optical coherence tomography (OCT) in thickness and stiffness before the local vibration intervention and also by Laser Doppler Flowmetry (LDF).
2. Participants will lay supine throughout the experiment.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Inotuzumab Ozogamicin works to prevent relapses after transplantation in adult high-risk B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia treated with the PETHEMA ALL-2025 protocol.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do patients receiving Inotuzumab ozogamicin post-transplantation suffer less relapses than those patients not receiving this therapy (control group) within the ALL-2025 protocol?
* Do patients receiving Inotuzumab ozogamicin show more adverse events and severe adverse events related with this treatment than those patients no receiving this intervention (control group)? Researchers will compare the relapse rate between patients receiving Inotuzumab Ozogamicin post-transplantation and patients not receiving Inotuzumab Ozogamicin post-trasnplantation within the ALL-2025 protocol.

Participants will receive 3 cycles of Inotuzumab Ozogamicin therapy. Treatment will be initiated from day +70 post-transplantation and a minimum interval of 30 days between consecutive administrations.
primary_outcomes: Efficacy of Inotuzumab Ozogamicin (InO) in the prevention of relapse in terms of the relapse rate

Efficacy of InO in the prevention of relapse in terms of the disease-free survival (DFS).

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to compare the recovery of knee muscle strength and function in adults aged 18 to 65 years with a fracture in the middle part of the shinbone. All participants are treated with an intramedullary nail, which is a metal rod placed inside the shinbone. The nail is inserted through a surgical opening either above or below the kneecap.

The main question this study aims to answer is:

Does the recovery of the muscles that straighten the knee differ between the suprapatellar approach, performed above the kneecap, and the infrapatellar approach, performed below the kneecap?

Researchers will compare participants who received the suprapatellar approach with those who received the infrapatellar approach. The treating surgical team chooses the approach as part of routine medical care. The researchers do not assign participants to either surgical approach.

Participants will attend routine follow-up visits at 3 and 6 months after surgery. During these visits, researchers will:

Measure the strength of the muscles that bend and straighten the knee and compare the operated leg with the uninjured leg Assess the participant's ability to sense the position of the knee Measure knee movement and thigh circumference Ask participants about knee function and pain in the front of the knee

The researchers expect that recovery of the muscles that straighten the knee may differ between the two surgical approaches.

primary_outcomes: Isokinetic Knee Extensor Muscle Strength
title: Comparison of Knee Muscle Function After Suprapatellar and Infrapatellar Tibial Nailing in Patients With Tibial Shaft Fractures

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the relationship between changes in respiratory mechanics and cerebral oxygenation in adult patients undergoing elective lumbar disc surgery in the prone position under general anesthesia.

Cerebral regional oxygen saturation will be monitored using bilateral frontal near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), while respiratory parameters including tidal volume, respiratory rate, peak airway pressure, plateau pressure, positive end-expiratory pressure, and dynamic compliance will be recorded from the anesthesia ventilator. Measurements will be obtained at predefined time points before and after positioning the patient prone and after returning to the supine position at the end of surgery.

No changes will be made to anesthesia, ventilation, medication doses, or surgical management for research purposes. All clinical care will be provided according to routine practice by the responsible anesthesia team. The study will investigate whether changes in respiratory mechanics during prone positioning are associated with changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation.
lead_sponsor: Sehit Prof. Dr. Ilhan Varank Sancaktepe Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in Cerebral Regional Oxygen Saturation (rSO2) During Prone Positioning
title: Pulmonary Mechanics and Cerebral Oxygenation During Prone Lumbar Disc Surgery

brief_summary:
This randomized crossover clinical study will evaluate and compare the accuracy and chairside time of two non-calibrated splinting systems, IoConnect and Scan Pro, for obtaining complete-arch implant digital scans. The study will include completely edentulous patients with four well-integrated implants connected to multiunit abutments.

Each participant will undergo complete-arch implant scanning using both systems, with the order of the scanning protocols determined by a computer-generated randomization sequence. The digital scans obtained with each system will be compared with a verified conventional implant impression used to establish a reference model.

The primary evaluation will focus on the accuracy of the implant scans by assessing linear and angular discrepancies between each experimental scan and the reference model. Chairside time required for the scanning procedures will also be recorded. The study will determine whether differences exist between the two non-calibrated splinting systems in terms of complete-arch implant scan accuracy.
primary_outcomes: Linear trueness of complete-arch implant scans
title: Accuracy of Complete-Arch Implant Scans Using Non Calibrated Splinting Scanbodies

brief_summary:
This study will test a Regeneron drug called REGN13089-M404-M2980 ("study drug") to see if it can help treat previously treated, advanced solid tumors (tumors that have grown and spread to different areas of the body).

The study is focused on advanced cancers that have more of a protein called mesenchymal epithelial transition factor (MET) on the surface of their cells than usual. The study drug works by binding to MET on tumor cells and delivering chemotherapy directly into those cells. This may stop growth of the cancer cells and kill only the cancer cells and not the other normal tissues in your body. However, some of the chemotherapy may still affect the normal cells and side effects can still occur.

The study is looking at:

* What side effects the study drug might cause
* How well the study drug works
* How much of the study drug is in the blood at different times
* If the body reacts to the study drug, in a way that may cause the study drug to not work as well
* What is the best dose of the study drug for treating previously treated, advanced solid tumors

Occurrence of Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)

brief_summary:
Cubital tunnel syndrome is a condition that occurs when the ulnar nerve, which runs along the inside of the elbow, becomes irritated or compressed. It can cause pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness in the hand and arm. The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate whether early surgery leads to better outcomes than a non-surgical treatment approach using an elbow night splint for mild-to-moderate cubital tunnel syndrome in adults.

This study aims to answer the following questions:

* Does earlier surgical intervention improve patient-reported pain, symptoms, and function more than treatment with an elbow night splint after one year?
* How do symptoms, function, nerve function, and ultrasound findings compare between the two treatments over two years?
* How often do people who initially receive treatment with an elbow night splint end up needing surgery?
* Researchers will compare early surgery with treatment using an elbow night splint to see how the two approaches affect symptoms and function.

Participants will...

* be randomly assigned to have surgery or to receive treatment with an elbow night splint.
* have a physical examination at each study visit.
* have tests of nerve function and ultrasound imaging of the elbow.
* answer questionnaires about their symptoms, pain, and arm and hand function.
* attend appointments at the start of the study, and at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years.
primary_outcomes: Change in Patient-Rated Ulnar Nerve Evaluation (PRUNE) Score from baseline to 1 year
title: Comparing Surgical and Nonsurgical Outcomes of Cubital Tunnel Syndrome

brief_summary: The AIDE-CP1 trial will test whether a decision support tool based on artificial intelligence (AI) can improve care for patients who come to an emergency department with chest pain. The AI tool uses the patient's age, sex, first blood tests and ECG to estimate the risk of a heart attack within 30 days and suggests what to do next. About 4,500 patients at five Swedish emergency departments will be included. The study will examine whether the AI tool can shorten time spent in the emergency department while maintaining patient safety. brief_summary:
Background and Rationale Sepsis affects 20 to 30 million people globally each year, with an estimated 48.9 million cases in 2017. Despite medical advances, it still carries a high risk of death. Since sepsis progresses rapidly, early treatment is essential. This includes not only starting antibiotics quickly but also managing fluid levels effectively. Research suggests that in sepsis, fluid problems are often due to poor distribution in the body rather than an actual lack of fluids.

Currently, fluid and blood pressure management is often based only on monitoring arterial pressure, which may not provide a full picture of what's happening in the patient's circulatory system. More advanced indicators like Stroke Volume, Cardiac Output, and Peripheral Vascular Resistance can offer better guidance to optimize treatment and improve outcomes.

New non-invasive devices such as NICaS (Non-Invasive Cardiac System) make it easier and faster to monitor these values. NICaS uses electrical impedance technology and is approved by both the FDA and CE. It is easy to use, does not require specialized training, and allows for a more personalized and accurate treatment approach by tracking key heart and circulation parameters in real time.

Primary Objective

The main goal of this study is to compare two treatment strategies for patients with sepsis admitted to medical wards, and see which one leads to better survival:

* Fluid and/or vasopressor therapy guided by non-invasive hemodynamic monitoring (using NICaS), based on values like Stroke Volume, Cardiac Power Index, and Peripheral Vascular Resistance.
* Standard fluid therapy based on the international Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines.

Secondary Objectives

* Use of vasopressors: Check which strategy leads to less frequent use of vasopressor drugs and shorter treatment duration with them.
* Kidney function: See which method is linked to fewer cases needing dialysis or kidney support.
* Timing of vasopressors: Understand if giving vasopressors earlier leads to better short- and mid-term outcomes, such as lower death rates after 30 days, fewer ICU admissions, and shorter hospital stays.
* Albumin levels and circulation: Track how blood albumin levels change with circulation status, to see if there's a link with fluid leakage (capillary leak) and risk of death.
* Fluid balance: Analyze how fluid gains and losses relate to changes in heart and circulation measurements.
* Microcirculation: Test if adding signs of small vessel (microcirculation) issues to the main heart and blood flow indicators improves predictions of how patients will do.
* Prediction scores: Investigate whether combining NICaS readings with common scoring systems like SOFA or APACHE helps doctors predict patient outcomes more accurately.
* Time to stability: Compare how quickly patients in each treatment group recover to a stable condition. According to Rosenthal and Kavic's criteria, a patient is considered stable when: -Their illness is improving -There's low risk of getting worse again - Organ support is stable - There's little chance of new problems arising - There are no major complications.

Conclusion This study aims to evaluate whether a more personalized approach using real-time, non-invasive hemodynamic monitoring can lead to better outcomes in septic patients compared to standard care. If successful, this method could help reduce deaths, complications, and treatment costs in sepsis management.
lead_sponsor: Regione del Veneto - AULSS n. 7 Pedemontana
primary_outcomes: All-cause mortality at 30 days
title: Non-invasive Hemodynamic Optimization of Sepsis in Internal Medicine: a Randomized Study Comparing Therapy Guided by Non-invasive Hemodynamic Indices Versus Standard of Care.

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter, observational cohort study enrolls 6,000 adults with sepsis and/or acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) at multiple hospitals in China. Clinical data, treatment information, biological samples, and follow-up data are collected to characterize patient features and outcomes and to establish a multicenter clinical cohort and biobank.

The study focuses on the clinical and biological heterogeneity of sepsis and ARDS. Longitudinal clinical data are integrated with information on organ function, inflammatory and immune responses, and multi-omics profiles to identify clinically relevant phenotypes and biological subgroups. Biomarkers associated with disease severity, organ dysfunction, treatment response, and mortality are explored, together with models for outcome prediction. Follow-up after hospitalization evaluates long-term survival and recovery, including pulmonary function, physical function, quality of life, and psychological health.
primary_outcomes: All cause mortality
EuroQol-5 Dimension-5 Level (EQ-5D-5L) quality of life assessment
title: Multicenter Prospective Cohort of Sepsis and ARDS in China

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if QL1706 (Iparomlimab/ Tuvonralimab)+ chemotherapy+ cetuximab/bevacizumab works to treat potentially resectable colorectal cancer patients with liver metastases in adults. It will also learn about the safety of this therapeutic regimen. The main questions it aims to answer are: Does QL1706+ Chemotherapy+ Cetuximab/Bevacizumab improve the 18-month progression free survival (PFS) rate of participants?

The study plans to enroll 90-102 patients, who will be divided into 2 arms based on the primary tumor location and genetic status.

Arm A: Patients with primary tumors located in the left colorectum and RAS ( Rat Sarcoma Virus ) and BRAF ( V-raf Murine Sarcoma Viral Oncogene Homolog B ) wild-type.

Arm B: Patients with primary tumors located in the right colorectum and/or RAS or BRAF mutant

The study consists of two phases: phase Ib ( safety run-in phase ) and phase II.
lead_sponsor: Cancer Institute and Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
primary_outcomes: 18-month Progression-Free Survival (PFS) rate in phase II
safety in phase Ib
title: The QL1706 Combined With Chemotherapy and Either Cetuximab or Bevacizumab in Potentially Resectable Colorectal Cancer Patients With Liver Metastases

brief_summary:
Nursing students may experience considerable stress related to academic demands, clinical training, adaptation to university life, and concerns about professional competence. First-year nursing students may be particularly affected as they adjust to both university education and the nursing profession.

Self-compassion refers to responding to personal difficulties, failures, or stressful experiences with kindness, understanding, and a balanced awareness rather than harsh self-criticism. Previous research suggests that self-compassion may support stress management and psychological well-being, and that self-compassion skills can be developed through structured interventions.

This study will evaluate the effects of a brief self-compassion intervention among first-year nursing students. The intervention consists of two weekly, 90-minute face-to-face group sessions that include education and guided self-compassion practices. The study will examine whether the intervention is associated with changes in self-compassion, perceived stress, and mental well-being. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and six weeks after completion of the intervention.

The findings may provide information about the potential usefulness of a brief self-compassion intervention for supporting the psychological well-being of nursing students.
primary_outcomes: Self-Compassion
title: Effect of a Brief Self-Compassion Intervention on Nursing Students

brief_summary:
Dental caries is the most prevalent chronic non-communicable disease in childhood worldwide. In Chile, the last nationally representative oral health survey was conducted in 2007 and reported a caries experience prevalence of 70.4% (mean dmft = 3.7) among 6-year-old schoolchildren. More than 15 years have elapsed without updated population-based data, limiting the evaluation of the national oral health targets established for 2020. The First National Child Health Survey (ENSI) did not include oral examinations due to operational complexity, perpetuating this critical information gap.

This cross-sectional, population-based study aims to estimate the prevalence, severity, extent, and activity of dental caries lesions in both primary and permanent dentitions in a nationally representative sample of 6-year-old schoolchildren in Chile in 2024/25, using ICDAS-ICCMS. A probabilistic, stratified, two-stage cluster sampling design will be implemented, stratified by school administrative dependency (public, publicly funded private, and fee-paying private schools) and rurality, across all 16 regions of Chile.

The estimated sample size is 2,421 schoolchildren (total selected sample: n = 2,882, including replacements), drawn from a sampling frame of 226,959 eligible first-grade students based on the 2023 Ministry of Education enrollment registry. In addition to the clinical oral examination, a structured questionnaire will be administered to parents and caregivers to assess sociodemographic characteristics, oral hygiene habits, fluoride exposure, dental care utilization, and school-based preventive interventions.

The findings will provide updated nationally representative epidemiological indicators to support the evaluation of the National Oral Health Plan 2021-2030 targets and to inform oral health policies and resource allocation in Chile.
primary_outcomes: Dental Caries Experience Prevalence
title: Dental Caries and Related Factors in 6-Year-Old Schoolchildren in Chile: National Evidence for Assessment and Decision-Making (6yOH-Chile)

brief_summary:
Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the tissues surrounding dental implants and may lead to supporting bone loss. Current diagnosis is mainly based on clinical and radiographic findings. However, these methods may not fully reflect the biological changes occurring around implants.

The purpose of this observational study is to evaluate whether peri-implant crevicular fluid (PICF), a biological fluid collected from around dental implants, shows different molecular characteristics in peri-implant health and peri-implantitis. Adults who have at least one healthy dental implant and one implant with peri-implantitis will be included.

For each participant, PICF samples will be collected from one healthy implant and one peri-implantitis implant. The samples will be analyzed using attenuated total reflection-Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy. These techniques provide molecular information about biological samples without requiring additional invasive procedures.

The study will compare the spectral profiles obtained from healthy and peri-implantitis sites and evaluate whether these profiles can distinguish peri-implant health from peri-implantitis. Relationships between spectral findings and clinical factors, including probing depth, bleeding on probing, suppuration, radiographic bone loss, smoking status, and diabetes status, will also be explored.
interventions: ATR-FTIR and Raman Spectroscopic Analysis of Peri-Implant Crevicular Fluid
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Performance of Raman Spectral Profiles
Diagnostic Performance of ATR-FTIR Spectral Profiles
title: ATR-FTIR and Raman Spectroscopy of Peri-Implant Crevicular Fluid in Peri-Implantitis

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicenter, observational cohort study designed to externally validate the Trauma-Related Immobilization-related Prophylaxis (TRiP(cast)) score in Tunisian adults with acute lower-limb trauma requiring immobilization and managed as outpatients. The study will assess the ability of the TRiP(cast) score to identify patients at increased risk of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE), including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.

A secondary objective is to evaluate adherence to prescribed thromboprophylaxis and to compare adherence between patients receiving low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and those receiving direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). Factors associated with treatment adherence, bleeding events, and thromboembolic outcomes will also be investigated.

Patients aged 18 years or older with acute lower-limb trauma requiring immobilization for at least 7 days will be enrolled consecutively and followed prospectively. The decision to prescribe thromboprophylaxis and the choice of anticoagulant will remain entirely at the discretion of the treating physician according to routine clinical practice. Study investigators will not influence treatment decisions. The results are expected to provide external validation of the TRiP(cast) score in the Tunisian population and improve risk stratification and thromboprophylaxis management in ambulatory patients with lower-limb trauma.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE)
title: TRiP-cast Score Validation and Evaluation of Adherence to Preventive Anticoagulant Treatment in Patients With Lower Limb Trauma Requiring Immobilization

brief_summary: This study evaluates the safety and effectiveness of the Novelrad Vascular Closure System (NVCS), a suture-mediated vascular closure system, in achieving post-procedure hemostasis in subjects undergoing interventional catheterization procedures through the common femoral artery using large-bore procedural sheaths.
primary_outcomes: Safety: Freedom from major complications of the target limb within 30 days following the NVCS and index procedure.
Effectiveness: Time to Hemostasis
title: Safety and Effectiveness Clinical Study of Novelrad Vascular Closure System (NVCS)

brief_summary:
Sports participation is strongly encouraged in children and adolescents, but intense training at early ages may reveal hidden heart conditions that increase the risk of sudden cardiac death. Pre-participation evaluation aims to identify these conditions before sports practice.

This observational study will evaluate children and adolescents enrolled in the São Paulo Olympic Program (Programa São Paulo Olímpico). All participants will undergo a structured medical interview, a standardized physical examination and a resting 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). Participants with borderline ECG findings, warning symptoms, abnormal physical examination findings or a suggestive personal or family history will also undergo a 3-minute step test (Harvard step test) with continuous ECG recording during exercise and recovery, in order to detect exercise-induced arrhythmias.

The main goal is to estimate the prevalence of potentially pathological ECG findings in this population. The study will also describe warning signs in the medical history, abnormal physical examination findings, step test results, and the referrals and confirmed diagnoses during follow-up.
interventions: Diagnostic Test: Step test (Harvard step test)
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of potentially pathological findings on resting electrocardiogram
title: Cardiovascular Pre-participation Screening in Children and Adolescents

brief_summary: This is a single-centre, randomized, double-blinded controlled non-inferiority trial that will be conducted at the Orthopaedic Department at Uppsala University Hospital, Uppsala. The aim of the study is to evaluate the performance of a dual mobility acetabular component with a Vitamin E-infused highly crosslinked polyethylene (VEPE) liner compared to a conventional polyethylene (PE) liner in adult patients with symptomatic osteoarthritis, osteonecrosis, or dysplasia of the hip requiring a hip replacement. The assessments will focus on early wear, cup migration, adverse events, and clinical outcomes. Measurements will be conducted using Computed Tomography Radiostereometric Analysis (CT-RSA) instead of traditional radiostereometric analysis. The study hypothesis is that the PE liner will be non-inferior to the VEPE liner in terms of early wear over a two-year period.
primary_outcomes: Wear performance
title: E-Type - Early Wear of Polyethylene Liners Used in DMC

brief_summary: This prospective randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluated the effects of multistrain probiotic supplementation in patients with stage II-III colorectal cancer undergoing neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Participants received either a multistrain probiotic or placebo twice daily for five weeks during chemoradiotherapy. The study evaluated changes in gut microbiota composition and diversity, as well as fecal short-chain fatty acids, inflammatory cytokines, zonulin, gastrointestinal symptoms, and quality of life. Participants were assessed at baseline, during treatment, at the end of treatment, and seven weeks after completion of treatment.
primary_outcomes: Gut microbiota composition and diversity
title: Probiotic Supplementation During Neoadjuvant Chemoradiotherapy in Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary: This clinical trial studies how well ultrasound/photoacoustic/elasticity (US/PA/E) imaging works for early identification of tumor response in patients with stage II-III triple-negative breast cancer receiving immunotherapy and chemotherapy before surgery (neoadjuvant). US imaging uses high-energy sound waves to look at tissues and organs inside the body. The sound waves make echoes that form pictures of the tissues and organs on a computer screen. PA imaging delivers laser light into tissue which produces ultrasonic waves which are then converted into images. Elastography (i.e., elasticity \[E\]) imaging uses sound waves to send vibrations into a specific organ and measures how fast those vibrations move. The vibrations move faster through areas of stiff tissue and a computer uses these measurements to make an image of those areas. Combined US/PA/E imaging using the Vevo F2 and Vevo LAZR-X20 devices may be safe and provide earlier information about tumor response to standard neoadjuvant immunotherapy and chemotherapy than current standard imaging.
conditions: Anatomic Stage II Breast Cancer AJCC v8
Anatomic Stage III Breast Cancer AJCC v8
primary_outcomes: Serial changes in the ultrasound/photoacoustic/elasticity (US/PA/E) imaging biomarkers
title: US/PA/E Imaging for Early Identification of Tumor Response in Patients With Stage II-III Triple Negative Breast Cancer Receiving Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy and Chemotherapy

brief_summary:
Open neural tube defects are congenital malformations associated with significant morbidity. Early detection during the first trimester remains a key challenge.

This retrospective monocentric study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance of fetal biometrics (biparietal diameter and abdominal transverse diameter ratios) and maternal serum markers (beta-hCG and PAPP-A) for early screening of open neural tube defects. The study will assess the predictive value of these parameters individually and in combination to define optimal screening thresholds applicable in routine clinical practice
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic performance of biometric ratios and serum markers
title: First-Trimester Screening of Open Neural Tube Defects Using Biometrics and Maternal Serum Markers

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the Ronnie Gardiner Method (RGM) works to improve cognitive functions in adults with Parkinson's disease (early to mid-stage). It will also learn about the secondary effects on speech, mobility, balance, and mood.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a 10-week RGM intervention improve cognitive aspects, speech (indirectly through improved breathing), mobility, and balance in participants with Parkinson's disease?
* How do participants experience the intensity, difficulty, and emotional impact of the RGM sessions?
primary_outcomes: change in cognition
title: Short Term Effects of a Multimodal Intervention With RGM on Cognition in People With Parkinson's Disease.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether botulinum toxin A (BTA) or autologous nanofat injection is more effective for treating male androgenetic alopecia. It will also assess the safety of both treatments. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does botulinum toxin A or nanofat produce a greater increase in total hair count after 6 months?
* How do the treatments affect terminal hairs, vellus hairs, hair shaft characteristics, and other dermoscopic features?
* What side effects occur with each treatment?
* How satisfied are participants with the improvement in their hair condition? Researchers will compare intramuscular botulinum toxin A injections with intradermal autologous nanofat injections in men aged 18 to 40 years with Norwood Hamilton grade II or III androgenetic alopecia.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive either botulinum toxin A or nanofat
* Receive one treatment session at the beginning of the study
* Have clinical, dermoscopic, and photographic assessments at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months
* Have changes in total hair count and other hair characteristics measured during follow-up
* Report any treatment-related side effects and their satisfaction with the result
primary_outcomes: Change in Total Hair Count
title: Efficacy of Botulinum Toxin A Versus Nanofat in the Treatment of Androgenetic Alopecia: A Comparative Clinical Trial

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of two-tier test-based virtual reality (VR) instruction on Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) learning outcomes among clinical nurses. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a two-tier test-based VR instruction group or a traditional interactive VR instruction group. Both groups will use tablet-based, non-immersive VR to learn and practice ACLS-related clinical scenarios.

The study will assess ACLS knowledge, ACLS skills, resuscitation self-efficacy, critical reflection ability, and cognitive load. Assessments will be conducted before and after the intervention, with follow-up assessments conducted one month later to evaluate the retention of learning outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Advanced Cardiac Life Support Knowledge
Advanced Cardiac Life Support Skills
title: Effects of Two-Tier Test-Based Virtual Reality Instruction on ACLS Outcomes Among Clinical Nurses

brief_summary:
Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent complication of critical illness and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Early identification of patients at risk of progressing to moderate-to-severe AKI may facilitate closer monitoring and timely implementation of kidney-protective strategies.

This prospective observational cohort study will evaluate the predictive performance of the Renal Angina Index (RAI) for the development of Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) stage 2 or stage 3 AKI in adult intensive care unit patients. Consecutive eligible patients admitted to the participating adult intensive care unit will be enrolled. The RAI will be calculated 24 hours after ICU admission using routinely available clinical characteristics and the change in serum creatinine between ICU admission and 24 hours.

The primary outcome will be the development of KDIGO stage 2 or stage 3 AKI during the subsequent 48 hours. AKI staging will incorporate serum creatinine, urine-output, and renal replacement therapy criteria according to KDIGO definitions. The predictive performance of RAI will be evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and the prespecified RAI threshold of ≥10.

Secondary outcomes will include 7-day and 30-day intensive care unit mortality, intensive care unit length of stay, and duration of invasive mechanical ventilation.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve of the Renal Angina Index for Predicting KDIGO Stage 2 or Stage 3 Acute Kidney Injury
title: Renal Angina Index for Predicting Acute Kidney Injury in Adult ICU Patients

brief_summary:
This research group has previously established a safe and reliable model of experimental human streptococcal pharyngitis (a 'strep throat' human challenge model). The CHIVAS-IgG study will use this model to understand the ways in which antibodies help protect humans against strep throat infections.

Carefully screened healthy adults who are at very low risk of complicated strep disease will be admitted to a clinical trials unit where they will be randomly allocated to receive a licensed commercial 'intravenous immunoglobulin' product that is a mixture of antibodies from thousands of humans, or a placebo ('saline' or salty water), by intravenous injection.

About a week after the injection of antibodies or saline, they will have strep throat bacteria (Streptococcus pyogenes) 'painted' with a swab on the back of their throat, as this research group has done previously for over 100 healthy adults. The participants will be observed closely for about 5 days to see if they develop symptoms (sore throat) and signs (red throat, big tonsils, sore glands) of strep throat. During that time, multiple throat and nasal swabs will be collected along with saliva samples, blood tests, and photos. Before discharge from the clinical trials unit, every participant will be treated with antibiotics to make sure any strep bacteria is removed.

Participants will return for study visits at about 1 week and 1 month later, to check on how they are feeling and to collect more samples to understand how their immune system responds to the strep challenge.

This study is an important step on the way to developing a vaccine to prevent strep throat, strep skin infections, and dangerous Streptococcus pyogenes diseases like invasive infections and post-infectious problems like rheumatic heart disease.
primary_outcomes: Acute symptomatic pharyngitis (disease) - proportion of participants in each arm who reach the study pharyngitis endpoint
title: Stopping Strep Throat With Antibodies in Healthy Adults.

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study evaluated the effects of an 8-week high-intensity interval training (HIIT)-based dual-task exercise program on attention, cognitive-motor performance, social adjustment, and quality of life in adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Thirty adolescents aged 13-17 years were randomized to an intervention group (n=15) or a control group (n=15). The intervention group completed 24 exercise sessions, performed three times per week for eight weeks, while the control group received no structured exercise program. Outcomes were assessed before the intervention, after the intervention, and at 3-month follow-up using the D2 Test of Attention, Stroop Test, BOT-2 Short Form, Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory, and Social Adjustment Scale.
interventions: High-Intensity Interval Training With Dual-Task Training
primary_outcomes: Attention Performance Assessed by the D2 Test of Attention
Strobe Test
Bruininks-Oseretsky Test of Motor Proficiency
title: Effects of HIIT and Dual-Task Training in Children With ADHD

brief_summary: This exploratory pilot clinical study evaluates the fit accuracy of cobalt-chromium removable partial denture (RPD) frameworks fabricated using conventional lost-wax casting and selective laser melting (SLM) at a 0° build orientation. Two partially edentulous participants with maxillary and mandibular Kennedy Class III modification 1 arches are included. Each participant receives four RPD frameworks: one conventionally cast and one 0° SLM framework for the maxillary arch, and one conventionally cast and one 0° SLM framework for the mandibular arch. Framework adaptation is evaluated using the silicone-replica technique and microscopic measurement of the gap between the framework and supporting oral structures at predefined locations. The study primarily compares framework fit between the two fabrication techniques and also explores differences between short- and long-edentulous-span sides and between maxillary and mandibular frameworks.
primary_outcomes: Framework-to-Tissue Gap Distance by Fabrication Technique
title: Clinical Fit of Conventionally Cast and 0° SLM Removable Partial Denture Frameworks
